Wider Sports News.title: ‘A really trusted asset class’: Why Palace and Newcastle’s shirt sponsors are backing the Premier League’s post-betting era
Wider Sports News.summary: The CMOs of Crystal Palace partner Temporal and Newcastle United backer Knox Hydrate explain how Premier League shirt sponsorship is opening new doors for their brands – and delivering more value than other marketing channels could. The post ‘A really trusted asset class’: Why Palace and Newcastle’s shirt sponsors are backing the Premier League’s post-betting era appeared first on SportsPro .
Wider Sports News.body:
The Premier League has just undergone its most visible commercial shift in a generation. Ahead of the 2026/27 season, more than half of English soccer’s top-flight teams were seeking brands to appear on the front of their matchday jerseys. In most cases, that prestigious slot had been vacated by a betting company.

A voluntary collective ban on front-of-shirt gambling sponsorship, which went into effect over the summer, has triggered a new wave of commercial dynamics. Betting brands were typically willing to pay a considerable premium for the international platform that Premier League shirt deals presented. For middle and lower-ranking clubs in a fiercely competitive division, the financial implications of that were impossible to overlook.

Wider Sports News.summary: One of European football’s longest-running kit partnerships is expanding beyond apparel, with the reported record agreement adding naming rights to Benfica’s academy and training base. The post Benfica and adidas extend partnership through 2033 in record deal worth reported €120 million appeared first on SportsPro .
Wider Sports News.body:
Sport Lisboa e Benfica and adidas have agreed a six-year extension of their partnership, continuing the longest-standing sponsorship relationship in Portuguese football, the club and the sportswear company announced on Monday.

The new agreement, which runs through 2033, is worth around €120 million, according to a source close to the deal – making it the biggest sponsorship agreement in Portuguese football history. Neither Benfica nor adidas officially disclosed the financial terms in their joint statement.

Wider Sports News.title: French soccer’s DTC dilemma: Why the LFP’s rights tender doesn’t mean the end of Ligue 1+
Wider Sports News.summary: With Ligue 1 reportedly set to resume talks over the next domestic rights cycle, Cyprien Castanedo, head of media platform and innovation at the LFP, explains why Ligue 1+ still has a part to play. The post French soccer’s DTC dilemma: Why the LFP’s rights tender doesn’t mean the end of Ligue 1+ appeared first on SportsPro .
Wider Sports News.body:
A year ago, Ligue 1 became the first major European soccer league to go almost entirely direct-to-consumer (DTC) in its home market with the launch of Ligue 1+. It was a groundbreaking move watched closely by the entire industry. But it was also an act of necessity, with the French Professional League (LFP) suffering from a collapse of the conventional market for its rights.

The early signs were encouraging, with a million subscribers signing up in the first month. Yet the future of Ligue 1’s great streaming experiment remains uncertain, with the LFP possibly planning for life after Ligue 1+ – at least as a primary distribution platform – already.

Wider Sports News.title: Why Big Bash League franchises are up for sale and what it means for franchise cricket
Wider Sports News.summary: After falling short with a proposal earlier this year, Cricket Australia is pushing on with plans to sell stakes in its Big Bash League teams. The post Why Big Bash League franchises are up for sale and what it means for franchise cricket appeared first on SportsPro .
Wider Sports News.body:
The boundaries of franchise cricket investment have been redrawn once again, circling another of the sport’s big three markets. Cricket Australia (CA) has confirmed plans to offer stakes to private investors in the eight teams from its domestic T20 competitions, the Big Bash League (BBL) and Women’s Big Bash League (WBBL).

Last week the organisation announced that its member bodies – each representing one of the six Australian states – could make their own decisions on selling shares under a ‘self-determination model’. The hope is that this raises up to AUS$1 billion (US$710 million) in fresh capital, most likely from groups with financial interests in Indian Premier League (IPL) teams and elsewhere on the global T20 circuit.

The post Liverpool’s UK£300m shirt deal shows airlines are doubling down on sponsorship – but who will it actually reach? appeared first on SportsPro .
Wider Sports News.body:
Last week, Liverpool reset the market for Premier League shirt sponsorship by announcing a record-breaking five-year deal with Turkish Airlines worth a reported UK£60 million (US$80 million) annually.

At a time when many categories are reassessing marketing spend, the airline sector is moving in the opposite direction, doubling down on sport and football in particular. Turkish Airlines is far from alone. Emirates has built a large part of its brand on the world’s most recognisable sponsorship assets through long-term partnerships with Arsenal, Real Madrid and a portfolio of major sporting events. Qatar Airways has invested heavily across football’s biggest properties, while Etihad continues to use Manchester City as a key pillar of its global marketing.

The Springboks coach spoke to local media as the South Africans confirmed they will play Fiji in Gosford on the NSW Central Coast next September, a final pre-Rugby World Cup hit-out for both sides two weeks before the tournament kicks off.

Both teams will be based on the Central Coast next year and the Boks have used the last fortnight to familiarise themselves with their 2027 RWC training base, while they rest up and recover from the four-Test Greatest Rivalry series against New Zealand.

Rugby.body:
Max Malins didn’t feel nervous. He’d put in the groundwork. Exclusive use of a Majorcaroof terrace had been secured. An overzealous restaurant manager recruited as accomplice. Phone wedged in a plant pot to capture the momentous seconds he’d ask partner Ella to be his wife.

As the couple gazed out across the sunlit hills of the Balearic island, Malins plucked the diamond ring from his pocket and began what’s best described as a torturous descent to the ground. His right leg jolted as if struck by a cattle prod. His knee buckled like a rotten tree trunk. For a beat, it looked like Malins was bound, head over heels, for the concrete. When the video was uploaded to Instagram, the boys back at Saracens had a field day in the comments.

Rugby.body:

Rugby.title: Gloucester choose another Welshman as captain for the 2026/27 season
Rugby.summary: Having been led by Tomos Williams last season, Gloucester have handed the captain's armband for the upcoming 2026/27 campaign to fellow Welsh international Dewi Lake.
Rugby.body:
Having been led by Tomos Williams last season, Gloucester have handed the captain’s armband for the upcoming 2026/27 campaign to fellow Welsh international Dewi Lake. Scrum-half Williams’ departure to Saracens left Gloucester needing an alternative captain and they have turned to Lake, who has plenty of leadership experience for both his former club the Ospreys and at international level.

Lake has captained Wales in 22 of his 36 Tests and filled in for the injured Jac Morgan during the Six Nations and the Nations Championship. The 27-year-old will be supported by two vice captains: England centre, Seb Atkinson, and fellow summer signing and old Ospreys teammate, Morgan.

Rugby.title: Exeter boss Rob Baxter gives insight into Henry Slade contract negotiations
Rugby.summary: Slade, 34, who has made 268 appearances for the Chiefs, is one of the last remaining members of the side that won the PREM and Champions Cup double six years ago.
Rugby.body:
Exeter Chiefs boss Rob Baxter says he will sit down in the next month with England outside centre Henry Slade to discuss him taking up the option for a second year in his current deal.

Slade, 34, who has made 268 appearances for the Chiefs, is one of the last remaining members of the side that won the PREM and Champions Cup double six years ago. And Baxter says that there are loads of reasons why Slade, who has won 78 England caps and started his career on a dual-registration at Plymouth Albion 15 years ago, will activate the clause and not finish his career with a lucrative move abroad or join one of their rivals.

Rugby.summary: Jack Willis could join Antoine Dupont in an exclusive club next week after the Toulouse flanker was shortlisted for the Top 14 Player of the Season award for a second successive year.
Rugby.body:
Jack Willis could join Antoine Dupont in an exclusive club next week after the Toulouse flanker was shortlisted for the Top 14 Player of the Season award for a second successive year.

The former England international is up against Bordeaux-Begles and France fly-half Matthieu Jalibert and ASM Clermont-Auvergne’s All Black Harry Plummer for the prize, which will be announced at the Ligue Nationale de Rugby’s Nuit du Rugby ceremony at the Olympia in Paris on September 28.

Rugby.title: New Springboks captain as Rassie Erasmus makes mass changes for Wallabies
Rugby.summary: Springboks coach Rassie Erasmus has made 13 changes to the starting side that defeated the All Blacks in Baltimore earlier this month.
Rugby.body:
Springboks coach Rassie Erasmus has made 13 changes to the starting side that defeated the All Blacks in Baltimore earlier this month, with Andre Esterhuizen set to captain the side for the first time against the Wallabies in Perth.

Erasmus has made mass changes to the side that secured a 3-1 series win in Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry, with Eben Etzebeth and Ethan Hooker retaining their spots in an otherwise new-look run-on side for the one-off Test.

Rugby.title: Henry Pollock signs new multi-year deal at boyhood club Northampton
Rugby.summary: The back rower has already amassed a career’s worth of accolades at the age of just 21 – boasting 49 Saints appearances, 13 England caps, a Lions tour and, most recently, a Gallagher PREM winners’ medal.
Rugby.body:
Northampton Saints have confirmed that England star Henry Pollock, one of the game’s most recognisable figures, will remain at his boyhood club after signing a new long-term deal.

The Lions back row joined Saints four years ago as a 17-year-old schoolboy and became the first rugby player to join Eddie Hearn’s Matchroom Talent agency earlier this year. He could celebrate his new deal by making his 50th Saints appearance against Newcastle Red Bulls, who attempted to lure him away from Franklin’s Gardens this weekend.

Rugby.summary: Henry Pollock has brought an end to his contract stand-off with Northampton, saying it was ultimately "a very easy decision" to sign an extension.
Rugby.body:
Henry Pollock has brought an end to his contract stand-off with Northampton, saying it was ultimately "a very easy decision" to sign an extension with the defending Prem champions.

"I am very, very happy to sign here," Pollock told BBC Radio Northampton. "I have been here my whole career so it made sense for me to stay on the journey with such a young group of players, who are so ambitious.

Rugby.title: Wallabies coach on ‘intensity’ expected from world champion Springboks
Rugby.summary: Australia assistant coach Tom Donnelly has likened the intensity of the Springboks to what the Wallabies will experience at Men’s Rugby World Cup 2027.
Rugby.body:
Australia assistant coach Tom Donnelly has likened the intensity of the Springboks to what the Wallabies will experience at Men’s Rugby World Cup 2027, drawing on the level seen during the Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry Series.

South Africa claimed a 3-1 series win against their opponents from New Zealand, which included a Test played in front of more than 68,000 fans in Baltimore. They have since flown from the United States to the east coast of Australia, and will head to Perth later this week.

Rugby.summary: "No, I agree with Mils. But I don't think you can drop someone out yet. I think Fabian Holland's definite to keep in there. I think he's one of the boys for the future who's doing exceptionally well," Putt said on his first appearance on The Breakdown.
Rugby.body:
With only two weeks to go until the Wallabies travel to New Zealand for the Bledisloe Cup series, former All Blacks captain Scott Barrett is racing the clock to be named in Dave Rennie’s 34-man squad.

Barrett hasn’t featured for the All Blacks since last year’s end-of-year tour, taking nearly a full season off Super Rugby Pacific on a non-playing sabbatical. His return was scheduled before the start of the Super Rugby Pacific playoffs with the Crusaders, but a back injury ruined any chance of pulling on the red-and-black shirt in 2026.

Rugby.summary: 73-Test prop Taniela Tupou believes the upcoming clash with the Springboks in Perth will be an important hit-out for the side.
Rugby.body:

Tupou started at tighthead prop when the Wallabies fought their way back for a memorable win at Johannesburg’s Emirates Airline Park 13 months ago, before the visitors went down swinging 30-22 in Cape Town the next weekend.

Rugby.summary: One of the three proposed options is a new competition to replace Super Rugby Pacific and the NPC with a 8-10 team competition, Cully reported on The Post.
Rugby.body:
The state of New Zealand Rugby’s Men’s domestic competitions is under review at this Thursday’s review summit in Wellington, according to The Post. Rugby journalist Paul Cully has reported that NZR and its stakeholders will discuss possible changes to Super Rugby Pacific and the Hilux NPC in Wellington.

A supposed three-option NZR document, which was shared with stakeholders and attendees of the national summit this Thursday in Wellington, was named “Men’s Elite Competition Possible Options”.

Rugby.summary: Wallabies backrower Charlie Cale has sustained a shoulder injury in the lead-up to the clash with the Springbok.
Rugby.body:
Wallabies backrower Charlie Cale has sustained a shoulder injury in the lead-up to the clash with the Springboks and is now set to return to Canberra. One-time Australia captain Nick Champion de Crespigny has been called into the squad for the first time under Les Kiss.

Cale has endured a tough run with injuries over recent seasons, having gone two years between appearances in Wallaby gold, before featuring in four Tests this season. But the loose forward has suffered another setback, as the Wallabies confirmed in a squad update on Tuesday.

Rugby.summary: "I really don’t think there’s anyone out there,” Wilson said on The Breakdown.
Rugby.body:
Former All Blacks winger Jeff Wilson believes that the Springboks have almost hit their ceiling under Rassie Erasmus, after convincingly beating Dave Rennie’s side 3-1 in the recent Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry series.

Erasmus has rotated heavily during the recent Rugby World Cup cycle to build a mountain of depth ahead of the 2027 tournament in Australia, but Wilson believes it won’t matter, as the Springboks can only have 23 players on the field.

Rugby.title: USA and Wales see World Rugby rankings bump after big WXV wins
Rugby.summary: Big wins over the weekend have seen both the USA Women's Eagles and Wales climb the World Rugby rankings.
Rugby.body:
Big wins over the weekend have seen both the USA Women’s Eagles and Wales climb the World Rugby rankings. Jack Hanratty’s USA have surged two places up the rankings thanks to their 40-36 win against Ireland.

The result against a higher-ranked opponent has lifted the Eagles above Scotland and Italy into sixth, one place behind Sunday’s WXV Global Series opponents, Ireland. At Tallaght Stadium the USA overcame a 19-point deficit to stun Scott Bemand’s side in Dublin with a second-half brace from Kathryn Treder, as well as tries for Hallie Taufoou and Freda Tafuna.

Rugby.summary: This weekend WXV Global Series Challenger 2026 heads into its final round - with Fiji and the Netherlands fighting for first place and a piece of silverware.
Rugby.body:
This WXV Global Series Challenger 2026 heads into its final round this weekend – with Fiji and the Netherlands fighting for first place and a piece of silverware. So, what permutations have we to consider? Let’s have a quick look at how the competition stands and what fans of each team can expect.

Heading into the final weekend, only two teams have a chance of winning the title, and those are Fiji and the Netherlands. Fijiana are well settled in first place with 10 points after successfully claiming two bonus-point wins, while the Netherlands follow in second place with nine and Spain in third with seven points.

Rugby.summary: Wales prop Sisilia Tuipulotu says selection for next year's inaugural British and Irish Lions women's tour is among her top rugby priorities.
Rugby.body:
Wales prop Sisilia Tuipulotu says selection for next year's inaugural British and Irish Lions women's tour is among her top rugby priorities. The in-form tight-head scored two tries in Wales' emphatic 50-19 victory over South Africa on Friday, under the watchful eye of Lions head coach Jo Yapp.

With Yapp saying she will only take the best players in each position, most of the touring party to New Zealand is expected to be made up of England's world cup-winning stars.

Rugby.title: Raffi Quirke's Newcastle career gets off to false start after injury setback
Rugby.summary: Newcastle Red Bulls boss Dan McFarland has confirmed that England scrum-half Raffi Quirke has been ruled out of the season opener against reigning Gallagher PREM champions Northampton Saints at Franklin’s Gardens on Friday night.
Rugby.body:
Newcastle Red Bulls boss Dan McFarland has confirmed that England scrum-half Raffi Quirke has been ruled out of the season opener against reigning Gallagher PREM champions Northampton Saints at Franklin’s Gardens on Friday night.

RugbyPass understands that Quirke, who moved from Sale Sharks this summer, has damaged knee ligaments and that the club have started to search for a potential replacement. The news will be a blow to Quirke, who suffered a string of hamstring and wrist injuries during his time with the Sharks and hoped a move to the North East would kick-start his stalled international career.

Rugby.title: India names 13-member senior women’s rugby sevens team for 2026 Asian Games
Rugby.summary: India names 13-member senior women’s rugby sevens team for 2026 Asian Games The News Mill
Rugby.body:
Rugby India has announced the senior women’s Rugby Sevens team that will represent the country at the 2026 Asian Games, scheduled from October 1 to 3 in Nagoya, Japan. The 13-member squad will compete in the Women’s Rugby Sevens event at the Paloma Mizuho Rugby Stadium.

India has been drawn in Pool B alongside defending champions China, Hong Kong, China, and Malaysia. The Asian Games present a significant milestone for India’s Women’s Rugby Sevens programme. India made its debut in this category at the Guangzhou 2010 Asian Games but missed the 2014 and 2018 editions. The team returned for the Hangzhou 2022 Games, finishing seventh.

Rugby.title: Leicester close in on another big piece of contract business
Rugby.summary: Leicester Tigers are closing in on another eve-of-season boost, with England scrum-half Jack van Poortvliet nearing a new deal.
Rugby.body:
Leicester Tigers are closing in on another eve-of-season boost, with England scrum-half Jack van Poortvliet nearing a new deal. Norfolk-born Van Poortvliet, 25, joined the Tigers academy at 12 and is in advanced talks with the club about putting pen to paper on a new long-term deal.

Rugby.summary: The No.8's current contract was due to expire next summer but the western province have moved quickly to secure the services of last season's Player of the Year.
Rugby.body:
Ireland international Sean Jansen has extended his stay at Connacht beyond the end of this season after signing a new two-year deal, which will run until at least 2029. The No.8’s current contract was due to expire next summer but the western province have moved quickly to secure the services of last season’s Player of the Year.

Jansen signed from Leicester in 2023 and has become a fan favourite at the Dexcom Stadium due to his ball-carrying ability and try-scoring performances. Last season he scored 12 tries in 20 appearances, while he also made an immense contribution in defence, coming third in the URC rankings for tackles made (219).

Rugby.title: New signing blow for Bath as prop delivers bad news
Rugby.summary: Jamie Bhatti's second spell at Bath has been derailed almost as soon as it has begun after the Scotland prop revealed he has broken his arm via social media.
Rugby.body:
Jamie Bhatti’s second spell at Bath has been derailed almost as soon as it has begun after the Scotland prop revealed he has broken his arm via social media. Bhatti posted an image of an x-ray revealing the fracture on his personal Instagram account, which has yet to be officially confirmed by the club.

The 33-year-old, who arrived in the summer on a two-year deal, suffered the injury 10 minutes after coming on against his former club Glasgow in Bath’s final pre-season game at Old Anniesland last Friday.

Pollock, who was offered a deal by Newcastle Red Bulls, has been closing in on a new contract with the Gallagher PREM champions for the last few weeks, despite saying last week in a pre-season media session that he was open to offers.

Rugby.title: URC 2026/2027 squads rated: Munster
Rugby.summary: Munster's squad for 2026/27 feels like one caught between cycles. Clayton McMillan's outfit remains capable of putting a highly competitive XV on the field...
Rugby.body:
Munster’s squad for 2026/27 feels like one caught between cycles. Clayton McMillan’s outfit remains capable of putting a highly competitive XV on the field, but a closer look at the depth chart reveals a group that is still searching for its next generation of talent and one that is light on marquee players.

There is quality in key areas. Tadhg Beirne remains world-class, Craig Casey is central to almost everything Munster do, and Jack Crowley, if he can get back to full fitness in 2027, is still the standout talent in the backline.

Rugby.title: 'I want people to know who Rodrigo Marta is' - Portugal's history-making Top 14 try machine
Rugby.summary: Once lax and unprofessional, Marta is now approaching half a century of Test tries, including the most famous score in Portuguese rugby history.
Rugby.body:
Rodrigo Marta scores tries. He has scored against Hong Kong China. He has scored against Switzerland. He has scored against most of the nations on the Rugby Europe scene. He has scored twice in one game against the Azzurri of Italy. He has scored a bucketload in the ProD2 in France at a rate of close to one every other match. Recently, Marta has scored five tries in three games at the start of this Top 14 season. And he scored the most famous try in Portuguese rugby history, a swan dive in the south of France which took the Lobos to the promised land.

At just 26 years old, the Section Paloise back has 42 Test tries. On rugby’s all time list of international scorers, he is above Damian Penaud and Adam Ashley-Cooper. Jeff Wilson, Christian Cullen and Brian O’Driscoll are a few ahead of him. Marta is seven tries adrift of a place in the top 10.

Rugby.title: URC 2026/2027 squads rated: Sharks
Rugby.summary: After a dismal United Rugby Championship campaign last season, when they finished 10th having ended the previous season third, the Sharks have embarked on quite a recruitment drive.
Rugby.body:
After a dismal United Rugby Championship campaign last season, when they finished 10th having ended the previous season third, the Sharks have embarked on quite a recruitment drive.

While JP Pietersen’s side have welcomed many players, they have also seen plenty leave, including several of Rassie Erasmus’ favourites for the Springboks. The result is a Sharks 67-man squad containing a large contingent of Springboks in their mid-to-late 30s, allied with a host of South Africa U20 internationals and recent Junior Springboks who have plenty of potential but are yet to fully prove themselves.

Rugby.title: Junior Springboks sensation Haashim Pead's new club revealed
Rugby.summary: Junior World Championship 2026 Player of the Year, Haashim Pead has left one South African team for another on the eve of the new United Rugby Championship season.
Rugby.body:
Junior World Championship 2026 Player of the Year, Haashim Pead has left one South African team for another on the eve of the new United Rugby Championship season. Scrum-half Pead, who lit up the tournament in Georgia, scoring six tries in the Junior Springboks’ title-winning campaign, made the decision to leave the Johannesburg-based Lions and continue his rugby journey in the Western Cape with the Stormers.

During his time in Johannesburg, he established himself as a standout talent, earning his senior domestic debut in the Currie Cup against the Vodacom Bulls followed by an international debut against the Newcastle Red Bulls in 2025.

Rugby.summary: World Cup winner Joe Worsley believes reigning champions South Africa have created the template that can take Georgia to the next level as they prepare to face the Springboks in next year’s Rugby World Cup in Australia.
Rugby.body:
World Cup winner Joe Worsley believes reigning champions South Africa have created the template that can take Georgia to the next level as they prepare to face the Springboks in next year’s Rugby World Cup in Australia.

Worsley, who will be part of the Georgia coaching group for a third successive World Cup campaign, played in three tournaments for England, including the 2003 triumph in Australia. Now, he is helping Georgia build up for another massive rugby challenge Down Under and the success of the Springboks, who are chasing a third successive title triumph, will be used to show the Georgian players how they can develop their game.

Rugby.body:

The 59-year-old has joined up with John Mitchell’s Red Roses set-up on a short-term deal ahead of the world champions’ WXV Global Series fixture with the Black Ferns at Allianz Stadium this weekend. He will remain with England until the conclusion of WXV Global Series.

Edwards left his role with Fabien Galthie’s team in the summer after nearly six years in the role. During his time in the role, France enjoyed Guinness Six Nations Grand Slam success in 2022 and back-to-back titles in 2025 and 2026.

Rugby.title: Canada proved against the Red Roses you do not always have to 'earn the right to go wide'
Rugby.summary: Canada's innovative and educated players disproved Warren Gatland's old maxim as they ended England's winning run in a thrilling WXV Global Series draw.
Rugby.body:
The first coach of standing in the professional game who uttered the phrase was Wales head honcho Warren Gatland. “You have to earn the right to go wide,” he claimed in the early years of his tenure. Since then, it has passed into common currency and become the mantra of collision-based footy.

Very few stopped to argue the toss because of the outstanding stream of results in Gatland’s first spell: a Six Nations title at his first tilt in 2008; then five more, including three Grand Slams in the course of his 12-year period in charge. Wales reached the semi-final of the World Cup twice, in 2011 and 2019, and even briefly held the number one ranking in the world.

Rugby.summary: Despite a 55-21 win against Japan, Italy head coach Plinio Sciamanna believes his team still have work to do.
Rugby.body:
After a 55-21 win against Japan in his first game as Italy head coach, Plinio Sciamanna believes his team has plenty of room for improvement. The Azzurre combined forward power with attacking flair to put Japan under sustained pressure as they began life under Sciamanna on a positive note.

After tries from Aura Muzzo and Alessandra Frangipani in the middle part of the first half, the Sakura Fifteen responded with converted efforts from Nami Asari and Asuka Kuge to briefly turn the tide.

Rugby.title: Cornish Pirates impress in opening day Doncaster win
Rugby.summary: Cornish Pirates get their Champ season off to an excellent start as they beat Doncaster Knights 45-19 at the Mennaye Field.
Rugby.body:
Cornish Pirates got their Champ season off to an excellent start as they beat Doncaster Knights 45-19 at the Mennaye Field. Replacement hooker Matt Pritchard scored four tries after the interval to add to three first-half scores as the Cornish side were one of three Champ teams to get a bonus-point win in their opening game.

“I’m really pleased," Cornish Pirates joint-head coach Alan Paver told BBC Radio Cornwall. "A full house at the Mennaye, the grass is looking green, the sun's out and you're always a little bit apprehensive first game of the season against a quality side.

Rugby.title: The three big takeaways from round two of Super Rugby Australia
Rugby.summary: Despite the results blowing out at the weekend, the Super Rugby AUS competition is definitely fulfilling its purpose.
Rugby.body:
Super Rugby AUS Round 2 has come and gone, and it delivered great running rugby, big hits, tactical and skillful play, as well as two thrashings. Overall, the NSW Waratahs are the biggest dog in the yard at the moment, with the Western Force not far behind in their ability to lure their opponents into a scrappy dog fight whilst finishing them off with flair on the edges.

The ACT Brumbies’ Super Rugby Pacific backline is grossly underperforming and is not being helped by their beaten pack. Their scrum is their clear shining light. The Queensland Reds continue to struggle with a flat attack and appear unable to get any sort of foothold of momentum in their games.

Rugby.body:
After his USA Women’s Eagles side overturned a 19-point deficit to beat Ireland 40-36 in their WXV Global Series opener, Skerries-born head coach Jack Hanratty hailed his young team’s resilience.

Rugby.title: 'I learned nothing': France coach Ratier unimpressed despite dramatic Wallaroos comeback
Rugby.summary: France head coach François Ratier claimed he learned nothing new about his team after they completed an unlikely comeback to beat the Wallaroos.
Rugby.body:
France head coach François Ratier claimed he learned nothing new about his team after they completed an unlikely comeback to beat the Wallaroos. In Aix-en-Provence, Ratier watched his team score 17 unanswered points in the second half to overcome Australia to win 29-26.

It is a result made all the more impressive when you consider that, at one stage in the first half, France were reduced to 11 players on the pitch. A wild seven minutes saw Ambre Mwayembe receive a 20-minute red card, while both Lea Champon and Léa Murie received yellow cards for high tackles and Cloe Correa received a straight red card for eye-gouging in a maul.

Rugby.title: Eagles switch attention to Wales after ‘setting the tone’ with Ireland win
Rugby.summary: The USA Women’s Eagles kicked off their WXV Global Series campaign with a statement 40-36 victory over Ireland at Tallaght Stadium in Dublin.
Rugby.body:
The USA Women’s Eagles kicked off their WXV Global Series campaign with a statement 40-36 victory over Ireland at Tallaght Stadium in Dublin. It was a pulsating 80 minutes of rugby, with Ireland taking a 24-12 lead into the break before the USA produced a remarkable second-half comeback. Four tries after the interval turned the game on its head and saw the Eagles hold their nerve to claim a memorable victory on Irish soil.

Kathryn Treder crossed twice in the second half, with Hallie Taufoou and player of the match Freda Tafuna also finding the try line as Jack Hanratty’s side secured a thrilling win that will provide plenty of confidence heading into the remainder of their WXV Global Series campaign.

Rugby.title: USA loss a game Ireland 'should have won'
Rugby.summary: Ireland head coach Scott Bemand says their defeat against USA in the WXV Global Series opener at Tallaght Stadium was "a game we should have won".
Rugby.body:
Ireland head coach Scott Bemand said their defeat against USA in the WXV Global Series opener at Tallaght Stadium was "a game we should have won". USA, led by County Dublin-born head coach Jack Hanratty, fought back from trailing 31-12 at one stage of the second half to score four successive tries and claim a 40-36 comeback win.

A loss of discipline in the second half contributed to Ireland's loss after their impressive first-half display, and Bemand was frustrated that they let the game slip out of their control.

Rugby.title: URC 2026/2027 squads rated: Leinster
Rugby.summary: Leinster head into 2026/27 in a slightly unusual position. For all the familiar talk of depth, production lines and international quality, this is a squad that feels...
Rugby.body:
Leinster head into 2026/27 in a slightly unusual position. For all the familiar talk of depth, production lines and international quality, this is a squad that feels a little less bombproof than in recent years. There is still exceptional strength in key areas, particularly at hooker, lock and back row, where Leo Cullen can call upon a wealth of proven Test talent.

But there are also genuine questions to answer across the front row, in midfield and out wide. The departures of James Lowe, Rieko Ioane, Ciarán Frawley and Luke McGrath have stripped away experience and versatility, while Rabah Slimani’s exit leaves renewed scrutiny on a tighthead position that has been a long-running concern.

Rugby.title: Welsh rugby's key signings ahead of new season
Rugby.summary: Four summer signings are tipped to make a big impact at Cardiff, Dragons, Ospreys and Scarlets in the 2026-27 United Rugby Championship.
Rugby.body:
Wales' regions may have seen more star names depart but the summer has also seen one of the most active recruitment drives in recent years. There were notable departures with the loss of Jac Morgan, Dewi Lake, Aaron Wainwright and Marnus van der Merwe.

And Welsh professional men's rugby continues to be hit by off-field uncertainty with the WRU committed to cutting the number of regions from four to three. But Cardiff, Dragons, Ospreys and Scarlets - now all signed up to the new participation agreement and an increase in annual budget - have made significant additions as they seek old heads and overseas talent to help develop young homegrown squads for the 2026-27 season.

Rugby.title: Waisea Nayacalevu makes drastic position switch on debut for new club
Rugby.summary: Former Fiji captain Waisea Nayacalevu will make his debut for Rugby Olympique de Grasse, but in an unusual role: at no.8 for the Fédérale 2 club.
Rugby.body:
Former Fiji captain Waisea Nayacalevu will make his debut for Rugby Olympique de Grasse, but in an unusual role: at no.8 for the Fédérale 2 club. Nayacalevu left Nissa Rugby after helping the club secure promotion to the Pro D2, scoring three tries in 11 appearances for the southeastern French side. However, when his centre contract wasn’t renewed, he was free to find a new club, and RO Grasse stepped in, signing the Fijian legend for an undisclosed number of seasons.

Fédérale 2 is the fifth tier of French club rugby, sitting below the Top 14, Pro D2, Nationale and Fédérale 1, and is a predominantly amateur competition, although some clubs also field semi-professional players.

Rugby.title: Fergus Watson: 'I grew up wearing my granddad's Scotland cap
Rugby.summary: The muscular Glasgow back took seamlessly to men's rugby and longs to follow in his grandfather's footsteps by playing for Scotland.
Rugby.body:
As a young boy in Biggar, Fergus Watson coveted his grandfather’s Scotland cap. Bill Watson is in his late seventies now but some 50 years ago, wore the thistle 10 times alongside such giants as Andy Irvine, Ian McLauchlan, Jim Renwick and Sir Ian McGeechan. He would later run the whole Scottish Rugby enterprise as CEO during the turbulent early years of professionalism.

More than two decades since leaving office, those connections are still felt by his 21-year-old grandson, a muscle-bound wing who should see meaningful action for Glasgow this season. Usually, the familial memories are warm. Sometimes, though, the ripples from the past hit different.

Rugby.title: Munster relying on youth and a discarded talent as fly-half crisis comes to a head
Rugby.summary: Besieged by injuries in the number 10 position, the Irish province are growing increasingly desperate as the new season looms.
Rugby.body:
Eighteen months ago, Charlie O’Shea climbed the steps of the main stand at Virgin Media Park in Cork to lift the Munster Schools Senior Cup. His proud mother, Hilary, had the honour of presenting him with the Garrett Fitzgerald Trophy as hundreds of Christian Brothers College students roared their approval. It was a fitting end to O’Shea’s senior cup cycle. He was CBC’s primary fly-half through fourth, fifth and sixth year, but lost 2023 and 2024 finals to local rivals, Presentation Brothers College. He would leave CBC as a Schools Cup-winning captain.

On Friday, O’Shea shone on his first start with Munster’s senior team against two-time Champions Cup winners Leicester Tigers, at the same venue where he hoisted the silverware aloft. The 20-year-old grew up playing for Dolphin and had 15 All-Ireland League appearances for University College Cork last season. He is the last fly-half standing between Munster’s senior and academy squads. The United Rugby Championship season has not even begun.

Rugby.title: All Blacks ‘need to get rid of ill-discipline and rediscover lost art of building pressure’
Rugby.summary: New Zealand used to squeeze teams into submission with 'weaponised excellence', in the same way the Springboks have just done to them.
Rugby.body:
After four Tests against a Springboks team that is becoming one of the all-time greats, the All Blacks have learned that their single biggest failing is they have lost the art of building pressure.

When they were the game’s leading team and chasing greatness between 2010 and 2019 the way South Africa now are, the All Blacks knew how to build and maintain pressure on their opposition by stacking repeat moments of calm, accurate and disciplined play.

Rugby.body:
Despite continuing their 100 per cent win record under Whitney Hansen, the Black Ferns believe they must make key improvements ahead of next weekend’s blockbuster against England.

Hansen’s side outclassed Scotland at Hive Stadium in Edinburgh on Sunday morning, 66-14, scoring ten tries to two in a dominant second-half performance. Scotland were no match for New Zealand’s brutality with ball in hand, while the Blacks Ferns’ electrifying outside backs proved why they can be so dangerous when given opportunities.

Rugby.title: Mitchell predicts 'greater things' for England as winning streak ends
Rugby.summary: Head coach John Mitchell says England's thrilling draw with Canada will inspire "greater things to come" from the world champions despite the result ending their record-breaking winning streak.
Rugby.body:
Head coach John Mitchell believes England's thrilling draw with Canada will inspire "greater things to come" from the world champions despite the result ending their record-breaking winning streak.

England had won their past 39 Tests before Saturday's fixture. Canada, who had lost their 13 previous meetings with the Red Roses on English soil, held England to a 26-26 draw in a nail-biting, physical battle at Exeter's Sandy Park.

Rugby.title: New Zealand cruise to victory over Scotland in WXV
Rugby.summary: Scotland suffer a second successive defeat in the WXV Global Series as New Zealand run out comfortable winners at Hive Stadium.
Rugby.body:
Scotland suffered a second successive defeat in the WXV Global Series as New Zealand ran out comfortable winners at Hive Stadium. The Black Ferns ran in 10 tries while the Scots struggled to contain the number two ranked team in the world.

New Zealand took no time at all to exert their dominance, punching holes in the Scottish defence before powerful prop Mo'omo'oga Palu blasted through to score. The Black Ferns set a tempo the Scots could just not live with, and another foray into the Scottish 22 resulted in a neat finish from lock Maama Mo'onia Vaipulu for the second try.

Rugby.title: The Red Roses four-year winning streak ends on 39 games with Canada draw
Rugby.summary: England’s four-year winning run came to an end as they were held to a 26-26 draw by a Canada side they beat in last year’s Women's Rugby World Cup final.
Rugby.body:
England’s four-year winning run came to an end as they were held to a 26-26 draw by a Canada side they beat in last year’s Women’s Rugby World Cup final. A thrilling eight-try game was level at the hour mark after Olivia Apps crossed for Canada in what turned out to be the final score of the contest.

England pushed for their 40th straight win in the closing stages but were held at bay by determined defending from the visitors at Exeter’s Sandy Park. New Zealand remain the last team to have beaten the Red Roses, in the 2022 Rugby World Cup final.

Rugby.title: 'We wanted to go for the win': Why Canada took a draw against the Red Roses
Rugby.summary: When Claire Gallagher booted the ball into touch at full-time of Canada's 26-26 draw with the Red Roses, there were boos at Sandy Park.
Rugby.body:
When Claire Gallagher booted the ball into touch at full-time of Canada’s 26-26 draw with the Red Roses, there were boos at Sandy Park. The sold-out crowd in Devon wanted to see a winner. Everyone across the world did. Even so, you could see the practicality in the world’s third-ranked side taking a first-ever draw against the team that bested them in the Women’s Rugby World Cup 2025 final.

It had been an enthralling WXV Global Series encounter between the two teams. From start to finish, they went blow for blow. Thankfully, we will get two more instalments of these foes battling it out in October in Toronto and Ottawa.

Rugby.title: Canada end England's 39-game winning run with frenetic draw
Rugby.summary: England's remarkable winning run comes to an end as they are held to a nail-biting 26-26 draw by Canada at Sandy Park.
Rugby.body:
England's remarkable 39-match winning run came to an end as they were held to a nail-biting 26-26 draw by Canada at Sandy Park. The Red Roses were unable to escape the clutches of a relentless Canada, who they beat in last year's World Cup final, with the two sides sharing four tries apiece in front of a raucous 14,573 crowd in Exeter.

Canada are the first team to avoid defeat against England since New Zealand beat them in the 2022 World Cup final, but John Mitchell's side are now unbeaten in 40 Tests. The draw also ended England's 100% home record against Canada, having won each of their previous 13 home meetings.

Rugby.title: Canada player ratings v Red Roses | WXV Global Series 2026
Rugby.summary: Canada have done what few teams have managed to do – stop England in their tracks.
Rugby.body:
Canada have done what few teams have managed to do – stop England in their tracks. Kevin Rouet’s side ended the Red Roses’ 39-match winning streak to end, with a pulsating 26-26 draw against the world champions at Sandy Park in the WXV Global Series.

Canada came out with a clear purpose: to put right the disappointment of their 2025 Women’s Rugby World Cup final defeat. From the opening whistle, they came out firing, matching England’s physicality, playing with huge attacking intent and refusing to let the Red Roses settle.

Rugby.title: Talking points: How Canada proved their point and ended England's winning run
Rugby.summary: Although the skies in south-west England were grey and dreary, the rugby at Sandy Park was electric, with Canada bringing the Red Roses’ 39-match winning streak to an end with a 26-26 battle that went right up until the 80th minute.
Rugby.body:
Although the skies in south-west England were grey and dreary, the rugby at Sandy Park was electric, with Canada bringing the Red Roses’ 39-match winning streak to an end with a 26-26 battle that went right up until the 80th minute.

Rugby.summary: England's 39-match winning run is over after the world champions drew 26-26 against Canada at Sandy Park.
Rugby.body:
England’s 39-match winning run is over after the world champions drew 26-26 against Canada at Sandy Park. It was a hugely engaging tie in which each team scored four tries, and a converted Olivia Apps try in the 58th minute meant that nothing separated the two teams.

To describe Sandy Park as ‘tense’ is a disservice to the word. For much of the contest, nothing could separate England and Canada in a repeat of the Women’s Rugby World Cup 2025 final.

Rugby.title: Talking points: Italy impress against Japan in WXV Global Series opener
Rugby.summary: Italy started life under Plinio Sciamanna with a dominant 55-21 victory against Japan in both teams' WXV Global Series opener.
Rugby.body:
Italy started life under Plinio Sciamanna with a dominant 55-21 victory against Japan in both teams’ WXV Global Series opener. It took just three minutes for Aura Muzzo to open the scoring when she latched onto a lofted ball. Four minutes later, Alexandra Frangipani was over the whitewash too.

Japan enjoyed a brief shift of momentum after the 10-minute mark as Nami Asari and Asuka Kuge, along with Maiko Nishi’s kicking, handed the visitors a narrow lead. A lead that did not last.

Rugby.title: Eddie Jones: 'A great story... he's going through a golden period'
Rugby.summary: Japan head coach Eddie Jones praised his side's "intensity in our defence" and set-piece dominance as the Brave Blossoms claimed the Pacific Nations Cup with a 20-15 win over Fiji in Tokyo on Saturday.
Rugby.body:
Japan head coach Eddie Jones praised his side’s “intensity in our defence” and set-piece dominance as the Brave Blossoms claimed the Pacific Nations Cup with a 20-15 win over Fiji in Tokyo on Saturday.

In a match played in greasy conditions at the Prince Chichibu Memorial Stadium, Jones conceded his side “couldn’t get our attack going,” and thus relied on their set-piece superiority, with the maul being an area of success.

Rugby.title: Japan end Fiji’s Pacific Nations Cup reign with hard-earned win in Tokyo
Rugby.summary: Japan have taken out the Asahi Super Dry Pacific Nations Cup 2026 title, beating defending champions Fiji in Tokyo.
Rugby.body:
TOKYO: Japan have taken out the Asahi Super Dry Pacific Nations Cup title, beating defending champions Fiji 20-15 in the 2026 final. The Brave Blossoms had lost to the Flying Fijians in the last two deciders, but snapped that streak in front of a vocal crowd on Saturday.

Fiji gave away eight penalties in the first half alone, which gave Japan plenty of opportunity to build phases in attack and chase points. But the Brave Blossoms ultimately went into the break down by two, having turned the ball over nine times.

Rugby.summary: South Africa head coach Rassie Erasmus has confirmed that Pieter-Steph du Toit and Damian de Allende have been released from camp ahead of the Springboks' clash with Australia next weekend in Perth.
Rugby.body:
South Africa head coach Rassie Erasmus has confirmed that Pieter-Steph du Toit and Damian de Allende have been released from camp ahead of the Springboks’ clash with Australia in Perth next weekend.

The pair, who started all four matches in South Africa’s Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry series victory over the All Blacks, where they both became centurions, have returned home in order to spend time with their families, with Erasmus saying they have sufficient cover in the squad.

Rugby.summary: Canada have beaten the USA Eagles 19-16 in an all-time classic, wrapping up third place at the Asahi Super Dry Pacific Nations Cup 2026.
Rugby.body:
Canada have beaten the USA Eagles 19-16 in an all-time classic, wrapping up third place at the Asahi Super Dry Pacific Nations Cup 2026. It was a nail-biter that came right down to the wire, but the Canadians did enough to claim their second consecutive win over their arch-rivals.

The Canadians set the tone early with some physical carries and high-tempo play, and looked to build on the foundations they had set. Canada were almost immediately rewarded for their strong start, with the USA conceding a penalty inside two minutes.

Rugby.title: Wales deliver performance of serious promise
Rugby.summary: Wales have set themselves a new standard after clocking up a half-century of points in their WXV opener against South Africa.
Rugby.body:
Wales have set themselves a new standard after an impressive eight-try victory over South Africa in their WXV Global Series opener. It was a score even the most optimistic of fans could not have predicted against a team who went into the match ranked 10th in the world, three places above Wales, but the 50-19 scoreboard shone bright under Cardiff's Friday night lights.

Sean Lynn's side have been dealt their share of criticism in recent years, and understandably so with a winless World Cup and three Six Nations wooden spoons. But they were unrecognisable in the Welsh capital as players shook off the shackles of the past and delivered a performance of real promise.

Rugby.body:
TOKYO: Two-time Super Rugby winner Seta Tamanivalu has been brought into the Flying Fijians matchday 23 for the Asahi Super Dry Pacific Nations Cup Final, with winger Manasa Mataele ruled out just before the match in Tokyo.

Tamanivalu joined the squad in Japan this week, with midfielder Kalaveti Ravouvou ruled out of the decider with an injury. 34-year-old Tamanivalu, who used to play for the All Blacks, is now set to represent Fiji for the first time since the 2025 PNC.

Rugby.summary: 18 of the 23 Flying Fijians selected for the Asahi Super Dry Pacific Nations Cup Final currently play club rugby for the Fijian Drua.
Rugby.body:
TOKYO: 18 of the 23 Flying Fijians selected for the Asahi Super Dry Pacific Nations Cup Final currently play club rugby for the Fijian Drua. Incredibly, some of the club’s all-time greats are among the five others named to take on Japan at Prince Chichibu Memorial Stadium.

Fiji captain Tevita Ikanivere will lead the national team into another Pacific Nations Cup decider, as they look to secure a three-peat. Ikanivere is no longer part of the Fijian Drua squad, having moved to Japan Rugby League One outfit Mie Honda Heat.

Rugby.summary: Assistant coach Neil Hatley sees winning the Asahi Super Dry Pacific Nations Cup 2026 Final in Tokyo as an “absolute priority."
Rugby.body:
TOKYO: Assistant coach Neil Hatley sees winning the Asahi Super Dry Pacific Nations Cup 2026 Final in Tokyo as an “absolute priority” for Japan, who will look to end Fiji’s reign as champions when the two teams meet in another decider on Saturday evening.

Fiji are chasing a third Pacific Nations Cup crown in a row, having claimed silverware when the finals were last held in Japan two years ago. They then repeated that success, taking out the title in Utah last year with a six-point win over Japan.

Rugby.title: 'I want people to watch what this team is about': Sean Lynn's rallying cry as Wales end wait for win
Rugby.summary: Sean Lynn afforded himself a pleased look at full-time after Wales' 50-19 victory over the Springbok Women.
Rugby.body:
Sean Lynn afforded himself a pleased look at full-time after Wales’ 50-19 victory over the Springbok Women. He took on the role of Wales head coach after guiding Gloucester Hartpury to Premiership Women’s Rugby dominance. The side claimed three league titles in as many years.

Since he first led Wales in the 2025 Guinness Women’s Six Nations, Lynn had only seen his team experience victory once in the 15 Test matches he had presided over. During this time, his team have received back-to-back wooden spoons in the Women’s Six Nations and were dumped out of Women’s Rugby World Cup 2025 at the group stage, where they finished with defeat to Fiji.

Rugby.body:
Wales returned to winning ways in emphatic fashion with an eight-try victory over South Africa at Cardiff Arms Park. The hosts had gone nine Tests without a victory heading into their WXV Global Series opener, with a tight contest predicted against a Springboks side ranked three places above them in the world.

But Sean Lynn's bold selections paid off as Wales attacked with a freedom and intent they have not produced for years. They were six tries to the good in a dominant first half, with the visitors made to pay for indiscipline.

Rugby.title: URC Champions Leinster name travelling squad for Rainbow Nation tour
Rugby.summary: Three uncapped players and two new signings have made the 41-man squad that heads to South Africa for the first two games of Leinster's URC title defence, against the Lions and Sharks.
Rugby.body:
Leinster have included the majority of their Ireland internationals in the 41-man squad that will head to South Africa for the opening two rounds of the BKT United Rugby Championship.

Jack Conan is the most-capped Leinster player in the group with 180 appearances for the province, and the No.8 is joined by the likes of back-row colleagues Josh van Flier and Jack McCarthy, props Andrew Porter and Tadhg Furlong, hookers Dan Sheehan and Ronan Kelleher, lock James Ryan, fly-half San Prendergast, centres Robbie Henshaw and Garry Ringrose and back-three trio Hugo Keenan and Jimmy and Tommy O’Brien.

Rugby.title: Canada keen to develop 'important relationship' with PWR clubs
Rugby.summary: Canada head coach Kévin Rouet has revealed his ambition to strengthen links between the national team and Premiership Women's Rugby clubs.
Rugby.body:
Canada head coach Kévin Rouet has revealed his ambition to strengthen links between the national team and Premiership Women’s Rugby clubs. Ahead of Canada’s WXV Global Series-opening win against Scotland in Edinburgh, the squad were joined by Trailfinders Women coach Barney Maddison in camp.

The 37-year-old – who coached the West London club to the PWR final last season – joined the squad as a guest coach ahead of Canada’s 64-26 win at Hive Stadium. Rouet already has Saracens director of women’s rugby Alex Austerberry and Loughborough Lightning head coach Nathan Smith as part of his Canada coaching set-up.

Rugby.title: 2026 WXV Global Series preview: Ireland
Rugby.summary: Largely as expected, Ireland were dominant at times against Italy, Wales and Scotland during the 2026 Guinness Women's Six Nations.
Rugby.body:
Largely as expected, Ireland were dominant at times against Italy, Wales and Scotland during the 2026 Guinness Women’s Six Nations. They threw enough punches when losing to France and England to suggest that they are on a path that may well lead to being properly competitive against those nations in the years to come.

The Scotland game was a fantastic way for Ireland to end their Women’s Six Nations campaign, playing arguably the best attacking rugby of the Scott Bemand era in front of a record crowd at the Aviva Stadium.

Rugby.title: Rugby's Greatest Rivalry finale lays foundation for new era for rugby in America before RWC
Rugby.summary: Five years out from RWC 2031, the final Test between New Zealand and South Africa helped win hearts and minds among the US audience.
Rugby.body:
“The USA is at the heart of World Rugby’s new strategic plan.” Word from World Rugby Chair Brett Robinson, who briefed a small group of journalists gathered in the Trust lounge at the Baltimore Ravens M&T Bank Stadium, ahead of the final Test match in Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry series.

“Our ambition for 2031,” Robinson continued, “is to ensure that the Rugby World Cup here in the US is the best we’ve ever delivered. Because it’s so important for our game to grow and fuel the sport.”

Rugby.title: Every single World Rugby rankings permutations that can happen this weekend
Rugby.summary: Kévin Rouet's Canada can reclaim second in the World Rugby rankings if they end England's 39-match winning run in Exeter.
Rugby.body:
Kévin Rouet’s Canada can reclaim second in the World Rugby rankings if they end England’s 39-match winning run in Exeter. The second weekend of WXV Global Series action sees a repeat of the Women’s Rugby World Cup 2025 final take place at Sandy Park. The North Americans will retake second from the Black Ferns, who would also have to lose to Scotland in this scenario.

John Mitchell’s England can improve their rating for the first time this year with a victory of 15 points or more against Canada. A win by that margin will see the world champions improve by a maximum of 0.25. It will be the highest any England team has ever been rated should their overall rating reach 98.34.

Rugby.title: Rachel Cullum helps Canada to FISU Rugby Sevens Championship
Rugby.summary: Rachel Cullum helps Canada to FISU Rugby Sevens Championship The Queen's Journal
Rugby.body:
Another Gael has shone on the international rugby stage. From Sept. 4 to Sept. 6, Rachel Cullum, ArtSci ’27, helped Canada win the International University Sports Federation (FISU) Women’s Rugby Sevens Championship in South Africa. FISU is an organization in which national teams comprised of all the top university athletes compete against each other.

The Journal sat down with Cullum to talk about winning the championship, as well as her time in South Africa. The team arrived a week early in South Africa to train at the Stellenbosch Academy of Sport training facility, which Cullum believes allowed the team to “connect as a group” and gain an advantage over the other teams who “flew right into the competition.”

Rugby.title: Saints better prepared for Prem title defence
Rugby.summary: Northampton director of rugby Phil Dowson tells the BBC's Saints Show that the club has better chance of defending their title.
Rugby.body:
Northampton Saints are better prepared for this season's defence of their Prem Rugby title than the last time they were champions, according to director of rugby Phil Dowson. Saints finished top of the table in 2025-2026, winning 14 of their 18 matches before beating Exeter 26-17 at Allianz Stadium to lift the trophy in June.

They had also won the title in 2024, but saw a host of top players leave the club including Courtney Lawes, Alex Waller, Lewis Ludlam and Alex Moon before finishing a lowly eighth the following season.

Rugby.title: Adams Verling handed Ireland debut for WXV opener
Rugby.summary: Connacht back row Jemima Adams Verling is handed her senior Ireland debut in Sunday's WXV Global Series opener against the United States in Dublin.
Rugby.body:
Connacht back row Jemima Adams Verling will make her senior Ireland debut in Sunday's WXV Global Series opener against the United States in Dublin. Adams Verling will line out at blind-side flanker in the back row alongside captain Erin King at open-side flanker and Women's Six Nations player of the championship Aoife Wafer at number eight.

The 20-year-old's ascension to the senior team comes after she impressed in the U18 Women's Six Nations in 2024 and last year's U21 Women's Six Nations while she has also been impressive for the Clovers in the Celtic Challenge.

Rugby.summary: Jemima Adams Verling will make her Test debut in Ireland's first WXV Global Series 2026 fixture of the autumn.
Rugby.body:

The 20-year-old is the only uncapped player included in Scott Bemand’s match day squad for Sunday’s match at Dublin’s Tallaght Stadium. She has previously been named in extended Ireland squads.

Rugby.summary: Italy go into the WXV Global Series in a state of flux. They have a new coach, new players have been blooded and while the side has risen through the rankings, many of the same problems remain.
Rugby.body:

Rugby.title: Canada captain still loses sleep over final loss to England
Rugby.summary: Canada captain Sophie de Goede says she still loses sleep over their World Cup final loss to England last year.
Rugby.body:
It is nearly a year since Canada lost the Women's Rugby World Cup final to England - but time has not been a healer for everyone. "Four to five nights a week I can't fall asleep because I'm still thinking about the final," says Canada captain Sophie de Goede, who is preparing to take on the world champions this Saturday at Sandy Park in Exeter.

So, is this match revenge for the side ranked third in the world? Canada head coach Kevin Rouet is keen to play this down: "Revenge is a good brand but they [England] won the final of the World Cup - that was the most important game to win, the next important games will be in the World Cup 2029."

Rugby.title: Ban confirmed: Canada prop learns fate after Scotland red card
Rugby.summary: Canada prop Brittany Kassil has been banned for three matches after her red card against Scotland in her team's WXV Global Series opener.
Rugby.body:
Canada prop Brittany Kassil has been banned for three matches after her red card against Scotland in her team’s WXV Global Series opener. The ban will be reduced to two matches upon the successful completion of World Rugby’s Coaching Intervention Programme.

As things stand, the 35-year-old loosehead prop will miss this weekend’s replay of the Women’s Rugby World Cup 2025 final against England, next week’s clash with France in La Rochelle and her team’s first home Test of October, against England at Toronto’s BMO Field.

Rugby.title: Ex-Wales scrum-half Lloyd Williams does retirement u-turn
Rugby.summary: The 36-year-old, who won 32 caps for Wales, made the decision to hang up his boots ahead of last season's play-offs.
Rugby.body:
Former Wales scrum-half Lloyd Williams has decided to sign a new deal with Worcester four months after announcing his retirement from the game. The 36-year-old, who won 32 caps for Wales, made the decision to hang up his boots ahead of last season’s play-offs, which ended with the Warriors winning the Champ in their first season back in professional rugby.

However, Williams has decided he still has some more rugby in him and is now available for selection for tomorrow’s game against Bedford Blues, a re-run of last year’s final. “It’s been a bit of a surreal week, but it’s been great coming back, seeing everyone and fitting back into the environment – everyone’s made me feel really welcome,” said Williams.

Rugby.summary: Former Ireland co-captain Sam Monaghan has been ruled out of the team's entire WXV Global Series campaign with an Achilles injury.
Rugby.body:
Former Ireland co-captain Sam Monaghan has been ruled out of the team’s entire WXV Global Series campaign with an Achilles injury. It means that the 33-year-old will miss home Test matches against the USA Women’s Eagles, Japan and tour fixtures against the Springbok Women in Cape Town.

Last year the second row returned from an ACL injury to feature at Women’s Rugby World Cup 2025. She will remain in camp to lend her experience to the group. “Sam has been really unlucky,” Scott Bemand, Ireland head coach, said. “She picked up an Achilles injury, so that will be this competition out for her.

Rugby.title: Saints drop plan for memorial wall for fans' ashes
Rugby.summary: The club says there has not been enough demand for the project.
Rugby.body:
A plan for a memorial wall that would have included the ashes of Northampton Saints rugby fans has been cancelled. The Saints Memorial Wall was to have been part of a wider development to enhance the fan village at the Prem Rugby side's Franklin's Gardens ground.

However, the club said initial demand "was not sufficient to support the long-term viability of the development". Supporters who have already paid will receive a refund, Saints said.

Rugby.title: URC trial adds new twist to hotly-debated Rugby's Greatest Rivalry tactic
Rugby.summary: The United Rugby Championship (URC) has decided to bring forward the deadline for team announcements in the upcoming 2026/27 season to 2pm on Thursday.
Rugby.body:
The United Rugby Championship (URC) has decided to bring forward the deadline for team announcements in the upcoming 2026/27 season to 14:00pm (UK time) on Thursday. “Rather than Friday and Saturday teams being announced on separate days, all 16 teams will now work to a coordinated Thursday announcement time. For Friday fixtures, the timing remains largely unchanged, while teams playing on Saturdays and Sundays will generally be announced around 48 hours before kick-off rather than 24 hours,” the URC said in a statement.

Previously, this might have seen as a minor, inconsequential change, but the protocol around team announcements was hotly debated during the Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry Series (RGRS) between South Africa and New Zealand.

Rugby.summary: Exeter boss Rob Baxter says the Prem club has been sharing knowledge with Premier League side AFC Bournemouth.
Rugby.body:
Exeter boss Rob Baxter has said the Prem club has been sharing knowledge with Premier League side AFC Bournemouth. The Chiefs were taken over by the Black Knight group, which also owns the Cherries, at the end of June, becoming the first US-based group to take control of an English Prem rugby side.

Exeter's heads of departments such as strength and conditioning, physiotherapy and sports psychology have since linked up with their peers at Bournemouth. Baxter hopes he and his coaching team can get together with Cherries boss Marco Rose and his backroom team soon.

Rugby.title: Fijiana keen to keep impressing after historic WXV Global Series Challenger victory
Rugby.summary: When match official Amber Stamp-Dunstan whistled for the final time in the Spain-Fiji clash, the Fijiana had made history by beating Las Leonas for the first time.
Rugby.body:
When match official Amber Stamp-Dunstan whistled for the final time in the Spain-Fiji clash, the Fijiana had made history by beating Las Leonas for the first time. The 38-32 win came dramatically, as the Pacific Islanders trailed for most of the game before pulling off a remarkable comeback in the final 13 minutes with tries from Rokowati Nabura, Salote Nailolo and Repeka Adi Tove.

Harlequins’ Manuqalo Komaitai, who came in when the team needed it most, was still elated by what they had pulled off against a formidable Spanish side. “It feels good, as we made history for our country by beating Spain for the first time! I am so proud of the team and the girls for putting in the work and the fight to get this result.”

Rugby.summary: Former Scotland scrum-half Mike Blair reveals his excitement after teaming up with Dave Rennie as New Zealand attack coach and the prospect of facing up against his home country.
Rugby.body:
Foreign coaches are about as rare in All Black rugby as the Maui dolphin and the Kakapo parrot, which makes Mike Blair a unique individual in the Land of the Long White Cloud.

Speaking on the BBC Scotland Rugby Podcast, Blair describes his new life as Dave Rennie's attack coach with the All Blacks, a high-profile and high-pressure job, a unique honour, all the more welcome because Scottish coaches in elite rugby are desperately thin on the ground.

Former PREM club Rotherham are unlikely to ever go full circle and reach the game’s highest level again, but they have shifted 90 degrees ahead of their return to the Champ after an eight-year absence.

After decades of not much changing at their Clifton Lane home ground, which hosted top-flight rugby in 2000/01 but was not deemed suitable in their second stab at it in 2003/04, there has been plenty going on.

Rugby.summary: Black Ferns captain Georgia Ponsonby says she will be "friends off the field and enemies on it" with her former Trailfinders teammates this Saturday when she faces them at the Hive as New Zealand take on Scotland.
Rugby.body:
Black Ferns captain Georgia Ponsonby says she will be “friends off the field and enemies on it” with her former Trailfinders Women teammates this Saturday when she faces them at the Hive as New Zealand take on Scotland.

Ponsonby played the entire 2025/26 season in England’s Premiership Women’s Rugby for Trailfinders, becoming friends with Scotland’s Emma Wassell and skipper Rachel Malcolm. The hooker will also be playing international rugby in Scotland for the first time as the Black Ferns play the Scots in their own backyard for the first time.
Rugby.copy:

Rugby.body:
Fly-half Gareth Anscombe is looking forward to perhaps the final playing project in his career after joining Scarlets for the new season. The 35-year-old left French club Bayonne without a new club in the summer, wondering where his future lay.

Rugby.summary: When the Ultimate Sevens Academy started back in 2013, few could have predicted that it would lead to a brand new global sevens competition.
Rugby.body:
When the Ultimate Sevens Academy started back in 2013, few could have predicted that it would lead to a brand new global sevens competition. It has been a long journey over the last 13 years, but the academy’s goal to develop sevens players in the UK has proven a fruitful one, expanding out into Europe and North America.

It has been at the crux of the development of the Ultimate Sevens, with Managing Director Barney Pascall excited to turn sevens into a supercharged pathway to get new fans and players into rugby, having started work with the academy in 2020.

Rugby.title: Fin Smith sets England autumn ultimatum to hit form
Rugby.summary: England fly-half Fin Smith says an under-par autumn would trigger fundamental questions about the team's direction.
Rugby.body:
England fly-half Fin Smith says an under-par autumn should trigger fundamental questions about the team's direction. The 24-year-old was asked by Rugby Union Weekly about the state of the team after a miserable Six Nations and a summer campaign that featured a 45-21 defeat by world champions South Africa, a 73-8 thrashing of Fiji and a narrow 31-24 win over Argentina.

"I am not going to sit here and say 'we are building' because that is what you will get every time. "We will honestly find out in the autumn. If we have a pretty ropey autumn, on the back of building some momentum over the summer, I think we will need to have a pretty hard look at ourselves."

Rugby.title: Olivia Apps: 'We rewatched the World Cup final
Rugby.summary: When Canada play England at Sandy Park this Saturday, it will be 357 days since the two teams met in the Women’s Rugby World Cup 2025 final.
Rugby.body:
When Canada play England at Sandy Park this Saturday, it will be 357 days since the two teams met in the Women’s Rugby World Cup 2025 final. It is a day that will live in the memory of rugby supporters for plenty of years, as 81,885 supporters piled in to Allianz Stadium to conclude the best-attended and most successful edition of the tournament ever.

While the memory is bright for many, for Canada, the memory carries a little more darkness. Beaten 33-13 in West London the side left the field knowing that they did not live up to the potential they had shown in the lead-up to the final.

Rugby.summary: Ireland hooker Cliodhna Moloney-MacDonald admits she has found the smaller ball being trialled in women's rugby "challenging" in the build-up to Sunday's game against the United States.
Rugby.body:
Ireland hooker Cliodhna Moloney-MacDonald admits she has found the smaller ball being trialled in women's rugby "challenging" in the build-up to Sunday's game against the United States.

World Rugby is trialling a size 4.5 ball - about 3% smaller than the size five used in the men's game, but the same weight - during September and October's WXV Global Series. England players May Campbell and Helena Rowland raised concerns before the Red Roses' win over Australia last week, while Wales wing Lisa Neumann spoke positively about the impact it has had on her passing.

Wales and Bristol back Louis Rees-Zammit said he will be a winger who can play full-back this season for club and country, after spending much of the last campaign in the number 15 shirt.

Rees-Zammit returned to rugby last summer after almost two years away, as he tried to carve out a career in the NFL, and under Bristol boss Pat Lam and Wales head coach Steve Tandy was deployed at full-back consistently from the autumn, rather than his former position on the right wing.

The 21-year-old, an England Under-20 player, was hurt in Exeter's opening pre-season game when they lost to Welsh side Scarlets earlier this month. It is the latest injury blow for Exeter, who will be without Italy lock Andrea Zambonin until November with a shoulder problem.

Rugby.summary: Reid returns with rugby sevens gold medal; Samantha Reid and Team Canada win FISU World University Rugby Championship in South Africa pictouadvocate.com

Rugby.summary: This weekend, rugby’s newest competition Ultimate Sevens gets back underway in Biarritz, with the second round of action hitting the European mainland.
Rugby.body:
This weekend, rugby’s newest competition Ultimate Sevens gets back underway in Biarritz, with the second round of action hitting the European mainland after it burst out of the blocks in Cardiff.

With the reception of Cardiff from fans, players, officials and more almost universally positive, Pascall knows the competition is on the right track – and is primed for an even bigger follow up weekend in the southern French city.

Rugby.title: 'Get the fear of your own tryline out of your heads'
Rugby.summary: Neil de Bruin never wanted to be a coach, yet is bringing radical ideas and fresh thinking to one of South Africa's biggest rugby beasts.
Rugby.body:
When Canan Moodie took a quick tap under his own posts, there was a visible jolt in the Bulls coaching box. They might have been 19 points up and cruising at home to Zebre, but there was a collective stiffening of spines, breath catching in throats as one of South Africa’s most exceptional talents called for the mark and set off at a gallop. While the coaches’ brows furrowed beneath their baseball caps, one man was punching the air.

Neil de Bruin is the team’s attack specialist. He’s been at Johan Ackermann’s right hand from Johannesburg to Osaka and back again. De Bruin is a free thinker; eager to innovate and wary of the formulaic patterns which can infect a rugby team. He is shaping the Bulls attack in ways which might seem radical to some of its traditional fanbase. Young, vibrant and knowledgeable, he delivers these messages with beguiling zeal.

Rugby.title: Ospreylia: How Welsh club turned to a land down under

Rugby.body:
Ospreys will have an Australian twang this season, but it was not until May that they opted to recruit from down under through necessity. Mark Jones could pick a starting line-up that is 33% Aussie in the 2026-27 campaign, which gets under way with a United Rugby Championship (URC) fixture against Sharks in Durban on Saturday, 26 September (15:00 BST).

The Australian invasion started in the summer of 2025 when lock Ryan Smith arrived to soften the blow of losing Adam Beard to Montpellier. He has been followed to west Wales by three Wallabies in back-row forward Liam Wright, centre Lalakai Foketi and wing Marika Koroibete, plus fly-half Lawson Creighton.

Rugby.title: The numbers behind All Blacks' high ball struggles and the tactical change needed
Rugby.summary: The 2026 Greatest Rivalry Series was defined by the All Blacks inability to control the catch area. Knock ons became scrums, lost contests became second chance opportunities for South Africa.
Rugby.body:
The parallels between 2009 and 2026 are well documented for the All Blacks, with the high ball security becoming the dominant issue following three losses to South Africa. Much like 2009, the Springboks won 3-0 over the All Blacks with Fourie du Preez and both Steyns repeatedly putting up high balls. The wingers at the time, Joe Rokocoko and Sitiveni Sivivatu, two Fijian speedsters known for lethal running, couldn’t secure possession enough. The Boks fed off the resulting errors, that gave set piece and piggyback territorial wins.

It sounds like a familiar story with the All Blacks needing to find similar solutions to the Springboks kicking game. Rugby.title: Paul Williams: 'The All Blacks can still leave you spellbound like no other team'
Rugby.summary: The Boks may dominate the set-piece and lie top of the world rankings, but the All Blacks have shown they are on a redemption arc
Rugby.body:
Another month in rugby ticks by and it has only consolidated the fact in my head that the Boks’ scrum is the best we’ve ever seen, but the All Blacks shouldn’t give up hope, when in possession, they can still reach parts other sides cannot reach. Meanwhile, whisper it, but Australia may soon have the world’s best lock and closer to home, Lloyds’ sponsorship is a powerful shot in the arm for English rugby in these cash-strapped times.

Everyone has bad days. Regardless of career, we all have days when things don’t go quite to plan. But the difference between the All Blacks and normal people is that they rarely have two bad days in a row. In that regard, they are unique in rugby and perhaps even unique in sport. The lowest the All Blacks have been in the official world rankings is fifth (August 2022); prior to that, the lowest they had ever been was third – third is a dream for most rugby nations. This tour of South Africa has been further proof of their excellence. With what many would consider a rather average playing squad, given their history of individual brilliance, they have been the Springboks’ equals in a series of test matches that will live long in the memory. That does not mean they have matched the Boks in every aspect of play – they have not. The Boks’ scrum, for instance, has far outperformed the Kiwis’. But New Zealand have offset that disadvantage with ball handling so silky it would get the nod from even the most difficult to please of silkworms.

Rugby.title: How Keira Bevan's positional change will give Wales 'another dimension'
Rugby.summary: Keira Bevan has spent much of her Wales career pulling the strings from scrum-half, but now, she has been handed the keys to the whole orchestra.
Rugby.body:
Keira Bevan has spent much of her Wales career pulling the strings from scrum-half, but now, she has been handed the keys to the whole orchestra. Head coach Sean Lynn has raised eyebrows by naming the experienced 83-cap international at fly-half, ahead of Wales’ WXV Global Series opener against South Africa at Cardiff Arms Park on Friday 18 September.

And judging by what Wales have seen from her so far, Bevan is not simply filling a shirt. She is making the position her own. Her move was helped by an impressive end to the domestic season with Bristol Bears, where her performance against Gloucester Hartpury caught the eye of the Wales coaching staff.

Rugby.title: Leicester fly-half Searle agrees new contract

Rugby.body:
Leicester Tigers and England A fly-half Billy Searle has signed a new contract with the club. The 30-year-old joined Leicester in 2025 from French club Agen and scored 217 points in 24 appearances in all competitions during his debut season.

His form earned him a nomination for the Prem player of the season award in 2025-26. Head coach Geoff Parling told the club website:, external "Billy has produced performances of great attacking intent and game management, but what's impressed me the most is the professionalism he's shown and his intent to keep improving."
