Rugby.body:
Harry Potter actor Oliver Phelps has been named as part-owner of Ultimate Sevens team, Atlantic Novas. The 40-year-old, who starred as George Weasley in the blockbuster eight-film series, cited the “equal footing” for men’s and women’s players as a reason for his investment.

Last weekend, the brand-new competition headed up by former England and Great Britain captain Tom Mitchell launched in Cardiff. On the first weekend of Ultimate Sevens action, Clan Tartan won the men’s tournament and Phelps’ Atlantic Novas were winners in the women’s event.

Rugby.summary: When Jack Hanratty took over as head coach for the USA prior to this year’s Pacific Four Series, it was clear that the Eagles were starting a journey firmly pointed towards Women’s Rugby World Cup 2033.
Rugby.body:
When Jack Hanratty took over as head coach for the USA Women’s Eagles prior to this year’s Pacific Four Series, it was clear that the Eagles were starting a journey firmly pointed towards Women’s Rugby World Cup 2033 on home soil.

Of course, there is a desire to build a strong squad to compete at the 2029 edition in Australia, but there is also a significant element of looking at the long game. With that in mind, you’d imagine Hanratty and his staff are reasonably happy to have secured two wins in his opening five matches so far this year.

Rugby.title: 'Liberated' Glen Young driven on by Rugby World Cup carrot
Rugby.summary: Having slipped down the national pecking order, there are now a slew of at least 10 locks jostling for Gregor Townsend’s attention.
Rugby.body:
Rugby World Cup 2027 may still be just over a year away, but its looming presence is already there in the bodies and minds of many a pro gearing up for the new season. The rested and freshly conditioned bodies, at least those not already carrying knocks, are somewhere approaching match-readiness as the United Rugby Championship and Gallagher PREM prepare for lift-off next week.

And despite the 12-month marathon to make it to the start line Down Under, minds are being sharpened by the prospect of participating in the next global rugby gathering. Edinburgh’s Glen Young is no different. It may be over two years since he won the last of his four Scotland caps – against Canada on his only Test start, before a torn pectoral muscle forced him home and a wretched season battling further injury hassles ensued.

Rugby.title: ‘Quins have under-performed... but with this set-up we can go on and do great things’
Rugby.summary: With Robbie Deans installed as performance director, flanker Jack Kenningham believes Harlequins can 'get back to where we should be'.
Rugby.body:
If there was a table for under-achievement in English rugby over the past four seasons, Harlequins would arguably top it. In terms of league finishes Newcastle are the failed state club, having propped up the rest for three of those seasons, but pre-Red Bull, the Falcons were operating on a budget so small it would no longer be allowed under the Prem’s salary floor policy.

Quins have enjoyed sufficient financial clout to spend up to the salary cap yet since the 2021 champions reached the play-offs the following season, they have finished no higher than sixth. The 2025-26 campaign’s last-but-one finish saw them fail to qualify for the Champions Cup for eight years.

Rugby.title: Revamped South African back line ready for WXV opener against Wales
Rugby.summary: The Springbok Women kick off their WXV Global Series campaign against Wales at Cardiff Arms Park this Friday 18 September.
Rugby.body:
The Springbok Women kick off their WXV Global Series campaign against Wales at Cardiff Arms Park this Friday 18 September. Laurian Johannes-Haupt and Franzel September, who were recently appointed as co-coaches, have revamped the backline and made one change to the pack that scored four tries against the Black Ferns in Johannesburg a couple of weeks ago.

The side will be captained by Babalwa Latsha, who her debut at Cardiff Arms Park in 2018, with Lindelwa Gwala and Sanelisiwe Charlie completing the front row. Vice-captain Libbie Janse van Rensburg, who scored a try in the Springbok Women’s last appearance at the same venue in 2021 and could extend her Test points record (221) in this match, gets the nod at 10, and will be joined by Felicia Jacobs in the half-back partnership.

Rugby.title: 2026 WXV Global Series preview: South Africa
Rugby.summary: If the past 12 months have taught us anything, it's that if a game of rugby lasted only 40 minutes, the Springbok Women would be Women's Rugby World Cup contenders.
Rugby.body:
If the past 12 months have taught us anything, it’s that if a game of rugby lasted only 40 minutes, the Springbok Women would be Women’s Rugby World Cup contenders. At Women’s Rugby World Cup 2025, South Africa went into half-time level with the reigning champions, having matched New Zealand’s physicality and disrupted their attack. The Black Ferns eventually pulled away to win 46-17, but the Springbok Women had shown that the gap was narrowing.

At FNB Stadium two weekends ago, the pattern repeated itself. South Africa, again, produced a powerful, competitive first half before New Zealand’s greater attacking variety and ability to exploit space took control. The Black Ferns won 52-20.

Rugby.title: Wales make huge selection call for WXV opener against South Africa
Rugby.summary: Wales head coach Sean Lynn has made a huge selection call for his team's WXV Global Series opener against the Springbok Women.
Rugby.body:
Wales head coach Sean Lynn has made a huge selection call for his team’s WXV Global Series opener against the Springbok Women. Keira Bevan has been named to start at fly-half against South Africa at Cardiff Arms Park. The 29-year-old, who is more regularly seen at scrum-half, will line up at half-back alongside Seren Lockwood. It is the first time that Bevan has started at fly-half for her country.

Lleucu George, who is Wales’ regular fly-half, is named among the replacements, where there is a 6-2 split. There are three potential debutants in the squad. Amy Williams has been named to start on the wing, while hooker Shanelle Williams and tighthead prop Elan Jones are on the bench.

Rugby.body:

Saracens prop Carre and Sale centre Keight have been recognised with respective men's and women's player of the season awards after impressive performances during struggling campaigns for both national sides.

Rugby.title: Bevan to play at fly-half in Wales' WXV opener
Rugby.summary: Keira Bevan is to switch half-back roles after being selected to play at 10 for Wales' WXV opener against South Africa in Cardiff on Friday.
Rugby.body:
Keira Bevan will switch half-back roles after being selected to play at 10 for Wales' WXV opener against South Africa in Cardiff on Friday. The 29-year-old has been training at fly-half during pre-season and will partner Seren Lockwood.

Wales' regular 10, Lleucu George, is named among the replacements, while Kayleigh Powell is no longer an option having been ruled out of the campaign with a hamstring injury. Head coach Sean Lynn has included three uncapped players in his matchday squad, with Amy Williams named on the wing having impressed in a two-try display in June's uncapped Barbarians fixture.

Rugby.title: Rugby's Greatest Rivalry
Rugby.summary: Halfway through the series, Rassie Erasmus' Springboks mended their ailing areas of play and doubled down on their strengths. New Zealand could not respond.
Rugby.body:
The All Blacks’ tour of South Africa has produced a series worthy of ‘Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry’. It has been full to the brim with drama and controversy on and off the pitch. Neither side can bear to mention the name of the other without a swear word muttered under the breath. And that is as it should be in the joust between the two greatest rugby nations on God’s green one.

What are the portents for South Africa and New Zealand on the final march towards a World Cup in Australia in just over 12 months? Has the tour influenced the future of the game for better or worse?

Rugby.summary: Las Leonas were close to landing an important win over Fijiana in round one of the WXV Global Series Challenger, but in the end the Pacific Island nation side managed a remarkable comeback to earn a 38-32 victory.
Rugby.body:
Las Leonas were close to landing an important win over Fijiana in round one of the WXV Global Series Challenger, but in the end the Pacific Island nation side managed a remarkable comeback to earn a 38-32 victory.

Rugby.body:
England winger Tommy Freeman has signed a new contract with Prem champions Northampton Saints, keeping him at Franklin's Gardens "for the foreseeable future". The 25-year-old made his Saints debut in 2019 and has gone on to make 118 appearances for the club across all competitions, scoring 79 tries.

He scored Saints' opening try in their 2024 Premiership final win over Bath and repeated the feat in their 2026 triumph over Exeter Chiefs. "Its a no-brainer in terms of the coaching staff we've got," Freeman told BBC Radio Northampton.

Rugby.title: Bristol fans can breathe a little easier over Kalaveti Ravouvou injury
Rugby.summary: News of Ravouvou's injury whilst playing for Fiji against Canada in the Pacific Nations Cup last weekend caused concern among Bears fans, who fear they could be in for another injury-hit campaign.
Rugby.body:
Kalaveti Ravouvou is only expected to be sidelined for three to four weeks with the leg injury that he picked up in Fiji’s 45-29 win over Canada in last weekend’s Pacific Nations Cup semi-final.

Ravouvou, one of the most destructive runners in the Gallagher PREM, started at inside-centre for the Fijians, partnering former Bristol centre Virimi Vakatawa. Playing with a heavily strapped left leg, the 28-year-old lasted 55 minutes, making just three carries, before being replaced by Tuidraki Samusamuvodre.

Rugby.title: What happens when the average person takes on a Red Roses preseason test?
Rugby.summary: As soon as I crossed the finish line, the only thing I wanted to do was lay on the ground. My lungs burned. It was impossible to escape the glare of the sun.
Rugby.body:
As soon as I crossed the finish line, the only thing I wanted to do was lay on the ground. My lungs burned. It was impossible to escape the glare of the sun. But I had finished.

Three weeks previously I received a text, out of the blue that read: “I have an idea for you… would involve you doing some running.” The idea was fairly simple; how would the average person, plucked from the street, fare doing a Red Roses fitness test?

Rugby.body:
Henry Pollock is determined not to blink first in his contractual face-off. Despite a deal with Northampton being close, amid reports of an agreement of about £400,000 a year,, external the back row stressed on Monday that his renewal was not signed.

Rugby.body:
Capped Wallabies lock Nick Frost has been named in the ACT Brumbies starting side for the second-round Super Rugby AUS clash with the Western Force in Perth. Frost joins debutant Tavita Loughland in an otherwise unchanged forward pack

Rugby.body:
Kayleigh Powell has been ruled out of Wales’ WXV Global Series campaign in the latest injury blow for Sean Lynn’s side. The Harlequins back has sustained a hamstring injury that will see her miss Test matches against South Africa, USA Women’s Eagles and Japan in September and October.

Last week it was confirmed by the Welsh Rugby Union that Donna Rose, Kelsie Webster and Hanna Tudor had all been ruled out of action for the next two months. 27-year-old Powell started in all five of Wales’ 2026 Guinness Women’s Six Nations fixtures at full-back and scored one try as the team picked up a third wooden spoon in a row.

Rugby.body:
Wales have been dealt another injury blow before their WXV Global Series campaign with Harlequins' Kayleigh Powell ruled out of the entire tournament. The 27-year-old sevens Olympian was a standout player at full-back during the Six Nations and impressed at fly-half when Wales ended their nine match losing streak against the Barbarians in June.

But she will sit out Wales' Tests against South Africa, USA and Japan after suffering a hamstring injury in training. Powell wrote on her social media that she was "absolutely gutted" to be missing the campaign, but has "every faith that this team will do great things."

Rugby.title: Founder believes event can help give rugby sevens a much-needed boost
Rugby.summary: Founder believes event can help give rugby sevens a much-needed boost Hillingdon Times
Rugby.body:
The London City 7s founder believes the event can help give rugby sevens a much-needed commercial boost by bringing the sport into the heart of the City. Dan James sees a unique opportunity to unite top-level rugby, businesses and new audiences under one roof when the tournament returns to the Honourable Artillery Company on Thursday.

And for James, he wants the event to become a significant fixture for both the sporting and business calendars and sees the collaboration as central to growing the game. “Rugby, and rugby sevens in particular, has always had a problem with properly commercialising itself,” he explained. “What we’re trying to do is give it a really good foundation to grow into a really serious on-pitch product.

Tennis.title: Davis Cup: Great Britain book place in Finals as Neal Skupski and Henry Patten victory over Ecuador
Tennis.summary: Davis Cup: Great Britain book place in Finals as Neal Skupski and Henry Patten victory over Ecuador Sky Sports
Tennis.body:
Great Britain wrapped up a straightforward victory over Ecuador to book their place at the Davis Cup Finals in November. After singles victories for Arthur Fery and Toby Samuel on Saturday at London's Copper Box, Henry Patten and Neal Skupski clinched the tie at the earliest opportunity with a 6-3 6-4 win against Gonzalo Escobar and Diego Hidalgo in the doubles rubber.

Britain therefore join three-time defending champions Italy, Canada, Czech Republic, South Korea and Austria in booking their spot for the eight-team event in Bologna. It is the first time Leon Smith's side have reached the quarter-finals since 2023, when they were beaten by Novak Djokovic's Serbia in Malaga.

Tennis.title: GB dominate Ecuador to reach Davis Cup Finals
Tennis.summary: Great Britain will play in the Davis Cup Finals for the first time since 2023 after claiming a 4-0 win against Ecuador in London.
Tennis.body:
Great Britain have reached the Davis Cup Finals for the first time since 2023 after sealing a 4-0 win in their qualifying tie against Ecuador. Henry Patten and Neal Skupski booked Britain's ticket to November's 'Final 8' event in Bologna with a 6-3 6-4 win over Gonzalo Escobar and Diego Hidalgo in the doubles at London's Copper Box Arena.

That gave Britain an unassailable 3-0 lead after wins on Saturday for Toby Samuel and Arthur Fery in the singles, before Harry Wendelken, a late call-up to the team after Cameron Norrie withdrew injured on Friday, wrapped up the best-of-five tie by beating Angel Veliz 6-2 6-3 on his competition debut.

Tennis.title: Hewett & Reid star as GB win fifth World Team Cup
Tennis.summary: Great Britain become World Team Cup champions for the fifth time as Alfie Hewett and Gordon Reid secure a 2-1 victory over Japan in Florida.
Tennis.body:
Great Britain became World Team Cup champions for the fifth time as Alfie Hewett and Gordon Reid joined forces to secure a 2-1 victory over Japan in Florida. Japan were the defending champions of the competition, which is the wheelchair tennis equivalent to the Davis Cup and Billie Jean King Cup.

However, Hewett and Reid ensured Britain got their hands back on the trophy with a 6-1 6-2 win in the deciding doubles match against Tokito Oda and Daisuke Arai. "We're really happy to get the title back," said Reid, who was also part of the World Team Cup-winning squad alongside Hewett in 2015, 2019, 2023 and 2024.

Tennis.title: She is the only player Emma Raducanu has beaten at a Grand Slam this year after missing Wimbledon and the US Open
Tennis.summary: She is the only player Emma Raducanu has beaten at a Grand Slam this year after missing Wimbledon and the US Open Yahoo Sports
Tennis.body:
Emma Raducanu will want to forget her 2026 Grand Slam season in a hurry. Raducanu won the US Open in 2021, becoming the first and only qualifier to win a Grand Slam title. The Briton has dealt with many injury issues since then, with a stress fracture in Raducanu's lower right leg forcing her to miss both Wimbledon and the US Open.

Raducanu also lost in the first round of Roland Garros this year, with her only Grand Slam victory coming at the Australian Open back in January. Raducanu came into this year's Australian Open with little expectation, as a foot injury had hampered her preparations for the new season.

The 24-year-old overcame nerves to fight back from a set down against Andres Andrade and put the hosts in front at London's sold-out Copper Box Arena. Tennis.title: 'You have to start somewhere'
Tennis.summary: Cameron Norrie will miss Great Britain's Davis Cup tie with Ecuador this weekend, with qualification for November's eight-team finals on the line.
Tennis.body:
Cameron Norrie will miss Great Britain's Davis Cup tie with Ecuador this weekend, with qualification for November's eight-team finals on the line. British number two Norrie felt pain in his arm during a practice session and will be replaced in Saturday's singles by world number 95 Toby Samuel.

"He wasn't able to accelerate on the ball like he wanted to," Davis Cup captain Leon Smith told BBC Sport. "It's nothing major, but there's still a lot of tennis to be played this year and with that in mind, we had to make the difficult decision to replace him."

Tennis.summary: Raducanu vows to 'enjoy the process' for comeback after ruled out of China Open and Billie Jean King Cup lbc.co.uk
Tennis.body:
Brit now World No. 89 but does not want to put too much pressure on herself Emma Raducanu has voted to "try and enjoy the process" as she prepares to make a tennis comeback after two more withdrawals from tournaments.

The British number two has fallen to 89th in the world, having been inside the top 32 earlier this year, having pulled out of Wimbledon and the US Open. The 23-year-old withdrew from the China Open and was left out of Britain's Billie Jean King Cup squad as a stress fracture in her right leg did not heal in time.

Tennis.body:
Jack Draper simply needs a break, but the question is how long his body forces him to be away from tennis. The 24-year-old Brit has called it a season, about a month before his 2026 season would have ended anyway. Will he be able to come back healthier in 2027? Maybe not.

His longest-term injury is to his left arm (Draper's dominant hand), and it is an unusual bone. He has chronic bruising from internal bleeding in his humerus. The ailment forced him to miss every Grand Slam event this year, and his former top-10 ranking has fallen all the way to No. 143.

Tennis.title: Six-time Grand Slam champion Salisbury retires
Tennis.summary: Former world number one doubles player and six-time Grand Slam doubles champion Joe Salisbury retires from professional tennis.
Tennis.body:
Former world number one doubles player and six-time Grand Slam doubles champion Joe Salisbury has retired from professional tennis. Londoner Salisbury chose this month's US Open as his final event and reached the semi-finals with his long-time partner Rajeev Ram, who had also decided to retire.

The venue was fitting, as in 2023 Salisbury and Ram became the first pair in history to win three consecutive US Open men's doubles titles. Salisbury is Britain's most successful men's doubles player of the Open era. He also won the 2020 Australian Open with Ram, and two mixed doubles titles with Desirae Krawczyk.

Tennis.title: Charlotte to host WTA Finals from 2027
Tennis.summary: The WTA Finals will take place in the American city of Charlotte from 2027 on a three-year deal.
Tennis.body:
The American city of Charlotte in North Carolina has been chosen as the new home of the season-ending WTA Finals. The WTA says it wants to create the "Super Bowl of women's sports" and is hoping the three-year deal will bring more stability to an event that has had six hosts in seven years.

A planned 10-year stay in Shenzhen ended after just one year, with Guadalajara, Fort Worth, Cancun and Riyadh all taking turns since. Crowds have often been disappointing. "The WTA has always owned the WTA Finals, but now we are going to operate it, too," said WTA chair Valerie Camillo.

Tennis.title: More than the Score
Tennis.summary: It's been 23 years since an American last won a men's Grand Slam singles title
Tennis.body: Ben Shelton's defeat by Alexander Zverev in the US Open final means it's now been 23 years since an American last won a men's Grand Slam singles title. That didn't seem likely when Pete Sampras and Andre Agassi ruled men's tennis - but what does it really say about America's place in the tennis world? More than the Score's Delyth Lloyd talks to former professional player Denis Kudla, who's now a coach at Maryland's Junior Tennis Champions Centre - the place where US Open men's semi-finalist Frances Tiafoe and women's doubles finalist Robin Montgomery learned the game. He tells Delyth about his journey through the US developmental system, and how he built a 16-year career that saw him play at all four Grand Slams. He also shares the lessons he's now instilling in young players, and the importance of role models in their development. Delyth's also joined by Ben Rothenberg, editor of tennis magazine Bounces, who talks about why US women have had much more recent success at Grand Slams than their male counterparts - and why he believes a breakthrough on the men's side could happen very soon. Draper missed the US Open, after losing in the first round in Montreal and Cincinnati last month - and was in tears during his defeat to France's Terence Atmane in Canada. "I am taking this time to reset and heal so when I return I am 100% ready to go," Draper posted on Instagram., external

However, a complicated injury made things incredibly challenging and since that moment I've been desperately trying to get back and feel as I once did on the court.

Tennis.title: Jack Draper ends season early due to injury, targeting 2027 return to ATP Tour
Tennis.summary: Jack Draper ends season early due to injury, targeting 2027 return to ATP Tour The New York Times
Tennis.body:
Jack Draper has said he will not play again in 2026 due to fatigue from a “complicated” injury and is targeting a return to the ATP Tour at the start of 2027. The 24-year-old Briton, ranked No. 155 in the world, announced the decision on Instagram on Tuesday after being limited to 15 competitive singles matches this season by a chronic elbow injury in his left, playing arm and a separate right knee injury.

The former world No. 4 first experienced pain in his left elbow during the 2025 clay-court season and later developed serious bone bruising which forced him to withdraw from the U.S. Open after his first-round victory. He returned for Great Britain in the Davis Cup in February before making his ATP Tour comeback in Dubai later that month.

Courses are less crowded, conditions are still excellent, and best of all, the weather is cooler across virtually every region of the country. Golf.body:
Not sure about you, but fall is one of our favorite times to play golf. Courses are less crowded, conditions are still excellent, and best of all, the weather is cooler across virtually every region of the country. That means chilly mornings followed by comfortable afternoons and plenty of opportunities to add or shed layers throughout your round. With the right gear, you can stay comfortable on the course from sunup to sundown!

Hoodies became acceptable golf attire a few years ago, and by the look of things, they’re here to stay. Made with soft, cozy knit fabric, this hoodie has just the right amount of stretch to let you move freely throughout your swing.

Golf.title: Srixon rethought its whole process for new ZXi RKT metalwoods
Golf.summary: The Srixon ZXi RKT drivers, fairway woods and hybrids are the result of a whole new development process that has already yielded a major win. The post Srixon rethought its whole process for new ZXi RKT metalwoods appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Srixon isn’t just announcing a new lineup of drivers; it’s a complete overhaul of how the company thinks about metalwoods. The new ZXi RKT line of metalwoods is the product of a brand new development process for Dunlop Sports (the parent company of Cleveland, Srixon and XXIO), which is now focusing on the Srixon brand as their main platform for metalwoods and irons.

“It was overall just like rethinking how we design woods and getting it more geared towards this market and kind of the PGA players,” Patrick Ripp, Srixon’s Tour Engineering Manager, told GOLF. “From there, we developed a whole Tour prototyping team and a lot of the engineers that work on that, were working with the Tour and other products and had good relationships with the players and good relationships with the reps and really just started solving the problems that we had seen.”

Golf.title: Is this the biggest hint yet that Bryson DeChambeau is done with LIV Golf?
Golf.summary: Is this the biggest hint yet that Bryson DeChambeau is done with LIV Golf? Today's Golfer
Golf.body:
Nobody truly knows exactly what Bryson DeChambeau is planning next. That much was clear at 1pm EDT on Monday, when DeChambeau finally dropped the curious announcement he had been promoting on his social media channels with the tease: “I’m coming home.”

Did DeChambeau mean “home” as in his old domain, the PGA Tour? No. Did he mean a return to one of his former equipment brands? Again, no. The two-times US Open champion was in fact revealing a new YouTube golf series on his channel called the ‘Backyard Games’, featuring a $100,000 prize and several high-profile golf influencers. These include Grant Horvat and Brad Dalke, as well as Wesley and George Bryan.

Golf.title: 2026 Presidents Cup rosters, records: Meet the U.S., International teams
Golf.summary: The 2026 Presidents Cup begins Thursday, September 24. View the U.S. and International team rosters and records here. The post 2026 Presidents Cup rosters, records: Meet the U.S., International teams appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
From left to right: Hideki Matsuyama, Sungjae Im, Scottie Scheffler and Russell Henley at the 2024 Presidents Cup. All four players are back again to battle at Medinah. The 16th Presidents Cup tees off this week at famed Medinah Country Club in Illinois, located approximately 30 miles northwest of downtown Chicago. The biennial event is yet another illustrious feather in Medinah’s host-course cap, adding to a resume that already includes three U.S. Opens (1949, 1975, 1990), two PGA Championships (1999, 2006), and a Ryder Cup (2012).

Heading into this week, the U.S. has a dominant 13-1-1 record over the Internationals since the event’s first playing in 1994. The Americans’ lone loss was the 1998 edition at Royal Melbourne GC, which the International team won by a score of 20.5-11.5. In 2003, the Presidents Cup was also famously tied with a score of 17-17 at Fancourt Hotel and Country Club in South Africa.

Golf.title: Inside Medinah Country Club's spectacular 100-year-old clubhouse
Golf.summary: Medinah Country Club's epic, century-old clubhouse still thrills, no matter how many times it has been experienced. The post Inside Medinah Country Club’s spectacular 100-year-old clubhouse appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Medinah Country Club in suburban Chicago is a shrine to golf, the host of three U.S. Opens (1949, 1975, 1990), two PGA Championships (1999, 2006), a Ryder Cup (2012) and this week, the Presidents Cup between the U.S. and International teams. It’s also a shrine to Shriners International, an American Masonic society known for its philanthropy, fellowship, fun — and red fezzes.

Shriners from Chicago’s Medinah Temple founded the club in 1924. The Shriners’ formal name, “Ancient Arabic Order of the Nobles of the Mystic Shrine,” helps explain why charter member and renowned architect Richard Gustav Schmid designed Medinah’s expansive, exquisite clubhouse in a Byzantine style, topped with minarets and classic Moorish architectural elements.

Golf.title: Rules Guy: Can I quickly mark a ball on a slope before it rolls back?
Golf.summary: If your ball is on a steep slope, can you mark it quickly to avoid it rolling backward? Rules Guy has the answer. The post Rules Guy: Can I quickly mark a ball on a slope before it rolls back? appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
The Rules of Golf are tricky! Thankfully, we’’e got the guru. Our Rules Guy knows the book front to back. Got a question? He’s got all the answers. If I hit a ball onto the green and it stops at the top of a slope, can my caddie run up and mark it before a gust of wind might make it roll back down the slope? – Rick Gacho, via email

Presumably you are tipping this looper well, yes? Indeed, your caddie — or even, dare we say, you — can run like the wind to prevent any breeze from blowing your ball away. Rule 14.1 gives a caddie the right to mark and lift a player’s ball on the putting green … assuming the ball hasn’t already started rolling. Just give him or her a little something, you know, for the effort.

Golf.body:
An exemption for the LIV Golf Order of Merit for The 155th Open at St Andrews next year “remains under review” until a 2027 schedule is confirmed by the circuit. The spot for the breakaway circuit is hanging in the balance after Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund withdrew its backing for LIV Golf earlier this year.

A decision on whether it is still merited will be based on what exactly CEO Scott O’Neil can come up with as a 2027 schedule for LIV 2.0. Meanwhile, a new Last Chance Qualifier, won this year by Englishman Joe Dean, will again be part of The Open Qualifying Series for the 2027 event.

Golf.title: Golf’s next megastar? And Miracle memories: 18 Presidents Cup thoughts
Golf.summary: Here are 18 Presidents Cup thoughts before the event at Medinah. Will Jackson Koivun take another step? Will 2012 be a story? And more. The post Golf’s next megastar? And Miracle memories: 18 Presidents Cup thoughts appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
MEDINAH, Ill. — Michael Phelps and I high-fived. Fourteen years ago here, at Medinah Country Club, swimming’s greatest of all time had been following the 2012 Ryder Cup from inside the ropes when his arms started working harder than they would in any pool. The Americans were surging at the finish of day one, and Phelps was slapping hands with anyone he could find to the left of the 17th hole — and his paw hit mine. It was a moment. I remember it. He sure as hell doesn’t. But I’m pretty sure we both left thinking Team USA would win, and I’m pretty positive we thought that even more so the next day.

Three pals and I had driven in on Tuesday night of Cup week. The previous October, one of them told us he’d won a ticket lottery, and he planned everything over an email thread that included Ian Poulter’s name in the subject line and I’ll leave it at that. Entry for the week — for the week — was $680, and I think that gets you in for a day now. We saw a couple practice rounds. We stood near Michael Jordan at one point. Phelps and I connected. I couldn’t leave him hanging.

Golf.summary: In case you needed another reason to never bet against Tiger Woods, Peyton Manning shared an epic story in a recent interview. The post Peyton Manning’s $100 golf bet with Tiger Woods revealed much about Tiger appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
With 15 major championships and 82 PGA Tour victories on his resume, Tiger Woods’ competitive prowess is already the stuff of legends. But that all-encompassing drive to win wasn’t just limited to recorded tournaments. As two-time Super Bowl champion and Pro Football Hall of Famer Peyton Manning recently explained to GOLF’s Michael Bamberger, Woods’ burning desire to beat his opponents extended to pro-ams too.

Manning sat down to chat with Bamberger over Zoom to talk about the tournament he’s chaired for six years but which has existed for 34: the Smith Cole, which is held at Cherry Hills Country Club and attracts pro-member teams from clubs like Cypress Point, Seminole, Augusta National and more, who are then paired with Cherry Hills pro-member teams for a three-day competition.

Golf.title: Robert MacIntyre blasts ‘ridiculous’ rule that sent him spiraling
Golf.summary: Robert MacIntyre was none to pleased with an embedded-ball ruling he received at the BMW PGA Championship on Sunday. The post Robert MacIntyre blasts ‘ridiculous’ rule that sent him spiraling appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Robert MacIntyre couldn’t have asked for a better three-hole finish at the DP World Tour’s big-money BMW PGA Championship on Sunday. Birdie. Birdie. Eagle. The four-under blitz at Wentworth moved MacIntyre to three under for his round and 13 under for the week, good for a share of 10th place. Still, after signing his card, the combustible Scotsman wasn’t exactly all sunshine and rainbows.

He had a gripe to air, and air it he did, to The Scotsman’s Martin Dempster. MacIntyre, who is ranked 19th in the world, was still stewing from what he described as a “ridiculous” ruling on the 11th, a par-4 on which his drive had found the left-center of the fairway. When MacIntyre arrived at his ball, he found it plugged — or at least semi-plugged — in another player’s pitch mark. The good news for MacIntyre was that a 2026 rule change seemingly meant that he’d be afforded relief for his submerged ball. The bad news: Model Local Rule F-2 includes an exception: If a referee determines that the pitch mark has been repaired in some way, the player will not receive relief.

Golf.title: Jacob Bridgeman's latest win couldn't have been any more 'different' than his first
Golf.summary: Everything about Jacob Bridgeman's second win was different from his hand-numbing maiden victory at Tiger Woods' event — except one thing. The post Jacob Bridgeman’s latest win couldn’t have been any more ‘different’ than his first appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Back in February, Jacob Bridgeman arrived at the 18th hole at Riviera Country Club on Sunday with his dreams in his grasp. He was leading the Genesis Invitational, Tiger Woods’ tournament, with one hole to play. His first PGA Tour win was within reach; he just needed to par the final hole to hold off a hard-charging Rory McIlroy.

In the end, Bridgeman, despite being unable to feel his hands, made a four-foot par putt to beat McIlroy by one and win his idol’s tournament. That win sparked a season for Bridgeman that saw him make 22 of 23 cuts, post 11 top-10s and finish fourth at the Tour Championship. All that led to Bridgeman being picked by captain Brandt Snedeker to represent Team USA at next week’s Presidents Cup.

Golf.title: Ex-pros dish on U.S. team golf failures: 'Overblown, overdone and overanalyzed'
Golf.summary: Several former PGA Tour pros opened up about the challenges facing U.S. team golf ahead of the 2026 Presidents Cup. The post Ex-pros dish on U.S. team golf failures: ‘Overblown, overdone and overanalyzed’ appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
PEBBLE BEACH, Calif. — Rocco Mediate is honest about his Ryder Cup future. Mediate knows his chances of a U.S. Ryder Cup team roster spot ended long ago — around the moment Tiger Woods’ final putt dropped in the Monday playoff of the 2008 U.S. Open. He never played on an American Ryder Cup team. Never competed for the stars and stripes. Never felt the pressure over a 6-footer to extend your match. And maybe that’s for the best.

“I would have been the antichrist,” he says with a grin. But Rocco knows golf. He’s played professionally for more than three decades, and has been obsessed with sport’s history and traditions for just as long. He might not know what it feels like to be inside the team room, but he knows that success and failure in golf are decided in unusual ways. And this week, at the PURE Insurance Championship out in Pebble Beach, he has some ideas on how the Americans can turn things around after consecutive Ryder Cup losses despite what many view as a talent advantage.

After an appetizer of the Walker Cup and Solheim Cup in the preceding weeks, golf fans have one more team event to look forward to: the Presidents Cup. And although the biennial team event has been lopsided throughout its history, it still offers plenty of intrigue.

This year, the U.S. Team is led by Brandt Snedeker against an International side led by Geoff Ogilvy as the two teams square off at Medinah Country Club outside Chicago. There are plenty of new faces that will make their team-golf debuts when they suit up for their respective sides, but one who is not new to the pressures of the Presidents Cup is Christiaan Bezuidenhout, who is making his third appearacne for the Internationals. Ahead of his return Presidents Cup appearance, the South African chatted with Colt Knost and Drew Stoltz of GOLF’s Subpar to share the inside scoop on all things Presidents Cup.

Golf.title: What average golfers can learn from Ryan Fox's swift pre-shot routine
Golf.summary: Ryan Fox won the 2026 Open Championship at Royal Birkdale — and he did so with one of the fastest pre-shot routines in golf. The post What average golfers can learn from Ryan Fox’s swift pre-shot routine appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
One of the biggest lessons recreational golfers can learn from Ryan Fox’s epic Open Championship win doesn’t lie in his swing, but rather in his process. Foxy’s mental coach, Karl Morris, boils it down to three key words: intention, attention and attitude.

Intention means being clear about the shot you’re trying to hit. Decide what you want the ball to do, then commit to that picture. Attention is about keeping your focus in one place. Instead of juggling swing thoughts, give your mind one key. Finally, attitude is how you respond after the shot. Fox showed remarkable acceptance throughout the Open, particularly after unlucky breaks.

U.S. President Donald Trump, who was spending time at the presidential retreat in Camp David, Maryland, near Washington, D.C. over the weekend, suddenly returned to the White House at 8 p.m. on the 19th (9 a.m. Korean time on the 20th). As the State Department issued a new security alert on the same day urging heightened vigilance for Americans in the Middle East, various interpretations emerged regarding Trump’s early return, but the White House did not provide an answer. Trump is scheduled to attend several bilateral and multilateral events next week in conjunction with the UN General Assembly in New York.

On that day, the presidential helicopter ‘Marine One’ carrying Trump landed at the South Lawn in front of the White House, and inside the helicopter, golfer Bryson DeChambeau and Mikayla Demeita, a former Canadian ice hockey player, were captured on camera. DeChambeau, who is active in LIV Golf sponsored by Saudi Arabia, is a prominent pro-Trump figure in the golf world. Immediately after winning the 2024 election, he celebrated Trump on stage wearing a MAGA (Make America Great Again) hat. Trump also appeared directly on DeChambeau’s YouTube channel. In July, during the British Open, a major tournament, DeChambeau protested a two-stroke penalty and mentioned, “I will call President Trump,” sparking controversy.

Golf.title: After $5B in Saudi backing, what’s next for bankrupt LIV Golf? - Al-Monitor
Golf.summary: After $5B in Saudi backing, what’s next for bankrupt LIV Golf? Al-Monitor
Golf.body:
After $5B in Saudi backing, what’s next for bankrupt LIV Golf? Saudi Arabia is likely to focus on hosting key sporting events and developing the esports scene after the failures of LIV Golf.

The PGA Tour said Tuesday that it is not currently considering a new pathway for LIV Golf players to return, further complicating the future of golfers who joined the Saudi-backed circuit. The setback comes as Saudi Arabia shifts its sports strategy toward hosting major events and away from costly efforts to build new leagues, following LIV Golf’s financial struggles, experts told Al-Monitor.

Golf.title: The surprising memories lingering from Tiger Woods' history-changing Pebble Beach blowout
Golf.summary: Tiger Woods' 2000 U.S. Open will celebrate its 27th birthday next June, but it remains at the top of mind for the players he beat. The post The surprising memories lingering from Tiger Woods’ history-changing Pebble Beach blowout appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
PEBBLE BEACH, Calif. — Ernie Els laughs as the question arrives. Of course he remembers. You remember your great moments at the major championships like you remember your loved ones. When you have a score better than 154 players in the field at the U.S. Open, you don’t forget it.

But Els also laughs because he knows nobody has really thinks about his better-than-154-players score at the 2000 U.S. Open at Pebble Beach. They think only about the name that appeared above Els’ on the enormous manual scoreboard on 17 Mile Drive on that June Sunday — Woods. And yes, they think about how the only guy Ernie Els didn’t beat changed golf forever.

Golf.title: Rory McIlroy's electric eagle finish put much more than BMW PGA title in his sights
Golf.summary: With a show-stopping finishing eagle on Saturday, Rory McIlroy has the BMW PGA title and much more in his sights on Sunday. The post Rory McIlroy’s electric eagle finish put much more than BMW PGA title in his sights appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Rory McIlroy said he’d need to do something special. After a scruffy week in his title defense at the Irish Open, McIlroy arrived at this week’s BMW PGA Championship at Wentworth in second place in the Race to Dubai standings, giving himself a real chance to win his eighth season-long title this fall and tie Colin Montgomerie’s record of eight Race to Dubai crowns. But while McIlroy is in second place, he’s almost 1,000 points behind Patrick Reed, who won twice earlier this year.

“Obviously I’m in a very fortunate position, I guess, to be going for an eighth Race to Dubai. I can’t believe I’m sitting here with seven. So, yeah, I’d love to give myself a chance again,” McIlroy said in his pre-tournament press conference. “Last week wasn’t a great week for me in terms of the overall points. Patrick had a good week, and I didn’t have such a great week. I’m going to try — I’m going to have to try to make up for that this week.”

Golf.title: 'Odd man out': Left off U.S. team, J.J. Spaun contending in England
Golf.summary: J.J. Spaun admitted he's playing the BMW PGA with "a bit of a chip on my shoulder" after being snubbed from the U.S. Presidents Cup team. The post ‘Odd man out’: Left off U.S. team, J.J. Spaun contending in England appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
J.J. Spaun is happy to be in England this week; he’s clear on that point. “My family and I actually vacation over here in the wintertime,” he said after the second round of the BMW PGA Championship, flagship event of the DP World Tour. “So any excuse to come to the U.K., and England, especially, we try to make it happen. It’s nice the way the schedule worked out for me this fall to be here.”

That wasn’t just a throwaway line to appease the local press; Spaun and his family really do love England. “We go to the Cotswolds in mid-December for a couple weeks and just kind of enjoy the English culture. We feel the Christmas spirit a lot when we are over here,” he said. “It’s a lot of fun, just my wife and my two children. We have a good time and hang out at the pubs and relax.”

Golf.title: At Biltmore, 2 dream weeks are unfolding. Only 1 can end that way
Golf.summary: Neal Shipley and Ben Kohles are both hunting career-changing wins at the Biltmore. But only one can reach their dream ending on Sunday. The post At Biltmore, 2 dream weeks are unfolding. Only 1 can end that way appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
When Neal Shipley’s week began, his goal for the PGA Tour’s FedEx Cup Fall slate was clear: put the pedal down if he wanted to keep his card and playing privileges in 2027. Shipley, 25, became a sensation when he notched low amateur honors at the 2024 Masters and starred in an episode of Netflix’s docuseries Full Swing. Since that week at Augusta, which included a final-round pairing with Tiger Woods, Shipley has been grinding his way to the PGA Tour. Last year, he won twice on the Korn Ferry Tour to finish fourth in the standings and punch his ticket to pro golf’s big time. But his rookie season has been far from what he imagined. He missed 9 of his first 10 cuts and only made 8 of 20 cuts in total. He did not record a top-25 finish on the season and entered this week’s Biltmore Championship in Asheville, N.C., — the first tournament of the FedEx Cup Fall season — sitting at 183 in the FedEx Cup standings.

Needing to finish in the top 100 to keep his card, Shipley faced a steep uphill climb to remain on the PGA Tour in 2027. The math was clear: he needed either to post several high finishes or win between now and the RSM Classic in mid-November. Otherwise, he would be headed back to the Korn Ferry Tour.

Golf.title: How can playing golf alone help your game? This book seeks to find out
Golf.summary: In author Gary Belsky's new book "Solo Golf," he seeks to find out how playing golf alone can help your game. The post How can playing golf alone help your game? This book seeks to find out appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
In an era dominated by optimization, playing golf alone offers something increasingly rare: unstructured learning. Solo golf pares the game down to its essentials. And without distractions, a golfer becomes more attuned to the game.

As Gary Belsky writes in his new book, Solo Golf: The Zen of Playing Alone and How It Can Transform Your Game, solitude creates a different relationship with golf — one rooted in mindfulness and experimentation. A solo round turns the course into a laboratory.

Golf.title: 10 surprising players already qualified for 'new' PGA Tour
Golf.summary: The 'new' PGA Tour system doesn't start until 2028, but dozens of pros are already qualified — and a few more are in limbo. The post 10 surprising players already qualified for ‘new’ PGA Tour appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Earlier this week, the PGA Tour rolled out its eligibility criteria for its revamped two-tier system launching in 2028. The top-tier “Championship Series” will feature fields of roughly 120 players and there will be cut-and-dry promotion and relegation at the end of each season.

In other words, things will be simple. They just aren’t just yet. One surprising thing is just how many players have already secured their spots in the 2028 season. Because this is happening in real time, some exemptions are being grandfathered in, which makes the details of the “transition year” that much more compelling. Even ignoring the “Career Milestone” category (more on that later) there are roughly 40 players already eligible. Let’s run through 10 we know are in — plus a couple giant question marks — to make some sense of what’s to come.

Golf.title: Scottie Scheffler's legendary coach breaks down his unorthodox swing
Golf.summary: No one knows Scottie Scheffler's swing better than his longtime coach, GOLF Hall of Fame Teacher Randy Smith. The post Scottie Scheffler’s legendary coach breaks down his unorthodox swing appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
When I watch Scottie Scheffler playing on the PGA Tour each week, I still picture him as an energized seven-year-old buzzing around the practice facilities at Royal Oaks Country Club in Dallas. Back then, he insisted on wearing long pants any time he came to the course. It’s what the pros wore, so Scottie made sure to emulate them — even in the downright oppressive Texas heat. It’s safe to say his practice in imitation paid off. With 22 Tour wins and four major titles (so far), he’s become one of the best players in the modern game and one of the fiercest competitors in all of golf.

What’s funny about Scheffler’s progression from spunky junior to collegiate All-American to World No. 1 is that his swing really hasn’t changed all that much since he was a kid. Sure, he hits it longer and makes a few more birdies, but the DNA of his move is exactly the same — unique footwork and all. When folks ask me how I’ve helped keep Scheffler playing at such a high level, all I can do is laugh. With a student as talented, disciplined and driven as he is, it’s easier than you might think.

Golf.title: Greg Norman Claims LIV Golf Deserves Credit for CBS, NBC's Improved PGA Tour Broadcast Amid Its Bankruptcy
Golf.summary: Greg Norman Claims LIV Golf Deserves Credit for CBS, NBC's Improved PGA Tour Broadcast Amid Its Bankruptcy Yahoo Sports
Golf.body:
LIV Golf made a bold, tech-savvy entrance onto the global golf scene. The league launched its inaugural event at Centurion Club in June 2022 with a broadcast built from scratch. It caught eyes, as expected, since the PGA Tour still relied on traditional broadcast channels. Although Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund has stopped funding the league and the league has moved into its next chapter, founding CEO Greg Norman maintains that it has changed the way the sport is played and presented on television.

"Look what the tour has done with innovation. What the networks have done. And NBC and CBS with their production and technology. It's all because of what we did, what we produced. James Watson and those guys in our production team did phenomenal jobs being innovative at how to show differently to the viewer," Norman said on Golf Digest's The Real Deal, with Bob Philion, when asked if LIV was worth it.

Golf.title: 5 pre-shot routine elements you should consider for your game
Golf.summary: GOLF Top 100 Teacher Kellie Stenzel shares the benefits of having a pre-shot set-up routine for your golf game. The post 5 pre-shot routine elements you should consider for your game appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
A great set-up routine is a way to put the most important parts of your setup together in an order that works best for each individual. In most of my full-swing lessons, establishing an individual setup routine is a priority. While there are many options, here are some parts you may want to consider for yours.

The practice swing should be a realistic swing taken far enough away from the golf ball that you are not inhibited by its presence. Taking a practice swing too close to the ball can produce an improper motion that may transfer into the actual swing. Be sure to create enough space to avoid this.

Golf.title: Bridges Cup 2026: Meet the U.S. and International teams
Golf.summary: The Bridges Cup returns for its fourth playing, at Trump Turnberry, next month. Here's who's representing the U.S. and International teams. The post Bridges Cup 2026: Meet the U.S. and International teams appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
The Bridges Cup is set to return for its fourth playing from Oct. 5-7, bringing together 24 accomplished male mid-amateurs from five continents in a fitting reflection of the global reach of elite amateur golf.

This year’s match will be played at Trump Turnberry in Scotland and will feature five sessions of match play (two four-ball and two foursomes matches contested over the first two days, and 12 singles matches on the final day) on the King Robert the Bruce and Ailsa courses. The Ailsa course is a four-time host of the Open Championship, with an illustrious roster of winners that includes Tom Watson, Greg Norman, Nick Price and Stewart Cink.

Golf.title: Jon Rahm made his feelings clear on constant LIV Golf questions
Golf.summary: Jon Rahm made his feelings clear on constant LIV Golf questions AOL.com
Golf.body:
Jon Rahm shared his feelings about being continually asked about LIV Golf and its status. Rahm is one of the breakaway league's biggest stars, and as such, he often is the one in front of the camera addressing LIV and what is occurring within the circuit. With LIV facing an uncertain future, Rahm has been asked by reporters about the fledgling league and what could be happening, admitting he understands that it comes with his position.

This revelation comes weeks after LIV filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection following the Saudi Arabian Public Investment Fund's withdrawal of funding. Speaking to reporters during the BMW PGA Championship, Rahm explained that he understood the job they had to do regarding asking about the formerly Saudi-backed circuit amid its uncertain future. "No. I understand you're all doing your job, I get it," the Spanish star said when asked if he was "fed up" with LIV-centric questions.

Golf.title: 'The golf course is going to get hurt': A shape-shifting Pebble Beach has players talking
Golf.summary: Pebble Beach is showcasing two major changes at this week's Pure Insurance Championship, and players have noticed them. The post ‘The golf course is going to get hurt’: A shape-shifting Pebble Beach has players talking appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
PEBBLE BEACH, Calif. — Pebble Beach has a problem, and it took Ernie Els one swing on Friday afternoon to recognize it. “If even I’m hitting a 3-wood all the way down there on 16, they’re going to need some length on the golf course,” Els said Friday. “Unfortunately, I know the USGA is trying to work on that golf ball, but it’s got to seriously happen quickly.”

Els was referring to the change that has everybody talking through the early portion of the week at this week’s Pure Insurance Championship: the 16th hole, where Pebble Beach removed a famous tree from the right side of the fairway and replaced it with several hundred square feet of fresh sod and a series of “ground under repair” signs.

Golf.title: Caddie quits on PGA Tour pro — midway through round
Golf.summary: Caddie Cliff Ellis walked out on pro Alejandro Tosti midway through the first round of the PGA Tour’s Biltmore Championship Asheville. The post Caddie quits on PGA Tour pro — midway through round appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
On his Instagram story late Thursday afternoon, the Argentine pro posted videos of what looked like him aboard a two-seat seaplane flying over the mountains near Asheville, N.C. — a quick joy ride between the first and second rounds of the PGA Tour’s Biltmore Championship Asheville. There was a post of him about to board. Another showed his plane to the side of a commercial plane nearing take-off. Others showed him in the air, and one showed that his plane touched down in a lake.

All of that, though, preceded another departure. On Thursday, Tosti and his looper, Cliff Ellis, started the Biltmore Championship on hole 10 at the Cliffs at Walnut Cove, played the back nine, then things got weird. As first reported by Golfweek’s Adam Schupak and then shown Friday on Golf Channel, Ellis stopped carrying Tosti’s bag — on his ninth hole.

Golf.title: Does team pressure trump major pressure? This pro would know | Subpar
Golf.summary: Christiaan Bezuidenhout joined GOLF's Subpar podcast to talk Presidents Cup pressure, what it's like hanging out with Si Woo Kim and more. The post Does team pressure trump major pressure? This pro would know | Subpar appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
South African star Christiaan Bezuidenhout thinks he has had a big enough sample size to know whether players feel more pressure in team events than at majors. Bezuidenhout , who is 32, was the guest on this week’s Subpar podcast, where much of the conversation focused on next week’s Presidents Cup at Medinah outside of Chicago.

“Yeah, it’s a lot different,” Bezuidenhout said. “Playing for 11 other guys, playing for the shield, playing for the captain, the vice captains, for me it just adds a little bit more pressure [versus majors]. To go out there and do your best, put a point on the board and win your matches and play well and stuff, all of that just adds a little bit of pressure.

Golf.title: This legendary pro just turned 100. Here are some of his secrets
Golf.summary: Teaching pro Bob Toski turned 100 on Friday. In his honor, here's his colorful and revealing GOLF Magazine Interview from 2013. The post This legendary pro just turned 100. Here are some of his secrets appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Ed. note: Thirteen years ago, I visited legendary teaching pro Bob Toski in Boca Raton, Fla. The goal: spend a day with the PGA of America Hall of Famer, at his home and on the range, to better understand what kept his mind sharp and his motor running. Toski was 87 then, and still crackling with energy and chat. If you’d told me then he’d live to 100, I would have believed you. That’s how vivacious he was. Well, Toski made it. On Friday, he hit the century mark, and still is flashing his trademark pep. According to a PGA Tour report, Toski is hosting his own birthday party, where he’s planning to tap dance for his guests. In honor of Toski’s 100th, we’ve re-published GOLF Magazine’s 2013 interview with him below.

Excerpted from the October 2013 issue of GOLF Magazine. For access to the entire GOLF Magazine archive, join InsideGOLF today. You don’t have to snoop for long around Bob Toski’s Boca Raton, Fla., home to realize that the 87-year-old teaching icon has really lived. A samurai sword rests in a sheath in the foyer, a vestige of the years Toski spread his gospel in Japan. Adorning the hallway: framed photos of Toski at the 1954 U.S. Open at Baltusrol and on the first tee at the 1955 Masters with his dear friend Sam Snead. On a kitchen wall, another treasured snapshot: of Toski’s late wife, Lynn. “She was a model,” Toski says, beaming.

Golf.title: McIlroy in mix heading into weekend at Wentworth
Golf.summary: Rory McIlroy stays in contention with a five-under 67 to sit four strokes behind second-round leader Ryan Gerard at the BMW PGA Championship at Wentworth.
Golf.body:
Rory McIlroy stayed in contention with a five-under 67 to sit four strokes behind second-round leader Ryan Gerard at the BMW PGA Championship at Wentworth. The Northern Irishman made three birdies in his opening five holes and recovered from dropped shots on the eighth and 16th by picking up four strokes on the back nine, including birdies on the 17th and 18th holes.

Reigning Masters champion McIlroy's hopes of winning a record-equalling eighth Race to Dubai title were also buoyed by the withdrawal of Patrick Reed after nine holes. The American, who currently leads the standings on the DP World Tour, had been well placed after the first round but was forced to retire through injury while nine-over par for Friday's round.

Golf.title: Who said summer is over? For golfers, September is where it's at
Golf.summary: This summer was way too hot, at least in the Northeast. So hot it killed a rite-of-summer, Joy o’ Golf. Now is the time to make up for it. The post Who said summer is over? For golfers, September is where it’s at appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
I think this is reasonable to ask: As orange is the new black or was, and 50 the new 40 (nodding at you, boss), is September, for those of us living in golfdom, the new July? Survey says yes, or this reporter does, anyway.

On Labor Day, at 5 p.m., my wife and I were on an ocean beach on my native Long Island. The season’s lifeguards all gathered ’round the stand, 15 or so, beaded necklaces ’round their necks, Mardi Gras-style. They blew their whistles collectively, a musical chorus and a distinct note the likes of which I had never heard before, and made a mad group dash into the gentle, warm surf on the modest waves of high tide. The rest of us beachside took a break from our books, castles, refreshments and lounging, stood and applauded in gratitude for these tanned and essential seasonal workers, Red Cross-certified and ready to do what AI cannot: pull a kid out of a riptide. They were calling it a day, a weekend — and a season.

Golf.title: It wasn’t just the PGA Tour that stood up to LIV Golf. So did the DP World Tour, and it’s set to reap the rewards
Golf.summary: It wasn’t just the PGA Tour that stood up to LIV Golf. So did the DP World Tour, and it’s set to reap the rewards Golf Digest
Golf.body:
VIRGINIA WATER, England — The call that changed the landscape of international golf came only days after the 2026 Masters. When a report surfaced that Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund was on the cusp of withdrawing its funding for LIV, Ben Cowen, the DP World Tour’s chief tournament and operations officer, called Cho Minn Thant, CEO of the Asian Tour, to bolster their existing discussions about working together again.

“Cho and I had kept in communication throughout the past few years, and I always said to him, ‘The time will come, I hope, when we will work together again,’” Cowen told Golf Digest this week at the BMW PGA Championship at Wentworth.

But Rahm made a swift exit after he signed for a 5-over 77 on Friday to sit dead last on the leaderboard on 11-over par. His 155 total for two rounds is his worst 36-hole score in 253 total events as a professional.

Golf.title: Rory McIlroy ruling puzzles commentators. Here’s why he caught a break
Golf.summary: In the first round of the BMW PGA, Rory McIlroy tugged his tee shot on 14 into a tricky spot. That’s when the rules took center stage. The post Rory McIlroy ruling puzzles commentators. Here’s why he caught a break appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
If you were tracking Rory McIlroy’s form earlier in the week at the DP World Tour’s BMW PGA Championship, you would not have been surprised to see him birdie five of his first nine holes at Wentworth on Thursday en route to an opening three-under 69. Really, you might have expected him to go lower, given in the Wednesday pro-am he made 10 birdies and an eagle and recorded the unofficial course record on the revered Harry Colt design. (Alas, pro-am scores don’t count in the record books.)

Sandwiched between McIlroy’s early run of birdies in the first round was an oddity: a ruling that left Sky Sports broadcasters scrambling for a copy of the local rules in play for the week. The head-scratching started after McIlroy tugged his tee shot on the par-3 14th well left of the green. The ball settled on a narrow strip of grass between a fence and cart path, leaving McIlroy a daunting, seemingly unplayable, lie.

Golf.body:
The personal launch monitor (PLM) category continues to be one of the most innovative in golf. New options come out all the time, so it’s often about picking the option that suits your needs the best.

You can chose between going with something more focused as a game to create a simulator or something more focused on being used on the range for practice and instruction. Your use might also impact how much you’re willing to spend. If you’re just looking for something to make a game in your basement or give simple feedback on the range, then you might spend something in the $500-$700 range. Looking for more advanced data and accuracy that can keep up with the Trackmans and Quad Maxs of the world? Then you’re looking at spending somewhere between $3,000-$5,000.

Golf.title: Pebble Beach course change draws scorn. But critics didn’t have full story
Golf.summary: Justin Thomas was among critics of Pebble Beach’s decision to remove a tree on the 16th hole. But the resort says it had little choice. The post Pebble Beach course change draws scorn. But critics didn’t have full story appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Justin Thomas is not the Lorax but he speaks for the trees. He thinks golf courses cut down too many of them. Thomas said as much this week in a social-media post, citing a hole on a famous course to underscore his point: the par-4 16th at Pebble Beach Golf Links.

At 400 yards from the tips, the hole plays gently downhill from the tee, followed by an approach over a gully and between goal posts of Monterey cypress trees. At least, it used to. In early September, Pebble Beach removed the tree on the right, which stood some 90 yards short of the green.

You can call it a friendly rivalry between Jeff Fujimoto and Simon Holt, the two captains at next month’s Bridges Cup. They agree on most things, like the fact they are thrilled the premier mid-amateur international team match-play competition is heading to a venue as prestigious as Trump Turnberry. And that the Bridges Cup, about to get underway for the fourth time, is instrumental in promoting mid-amateur golf and showcasing the players who balance work and family while still competing at a high level.

Golf.title: Inside the top secret DP World Tour deal that left LIV Golf stunned
Golf.summary: Inside the top secret DP World Tour deal that left LIV Golf stunned Today's Golfer
Golf.body:
Saudi Arabia’s shock retreat from LIV Golf did not just upend one golf tour in 2026. The Asian Tour, a key partner for LIV, was also left reeling when the Public Investment Fund announced it would be withdrawing its multi-billion dollar backing from the creaking league. The developments stunned the Asian Tour’s chief executive, Cho Minn Thant, who had been discussing a five-year renewal with LIV before snaring a dramatic deal elsewhere to salvage his circuit’s future.

The shake-up to the new world order, negotiated in private during the Open Championship at Royal Birkdale, saw the Asian Tour pivot away from LIV Golf and re-align with the DP World Tour and the PGA Tour. The partnership will see the Asian Tour co-sanction five tournaments with the DP World Tour, including the Hong Kong and Singapore opens, as well as earning pathways to the European circuit.

Golf.title: 5 best golf balls under $30
Golf.summary: Expensive balls tend to cater to better players who rely on specific performance characteristics. Taking advantage of those characteristics often requires a combination of higher swing speed, consistent contact and the ability to control launch and spin. The post 5 best golf balls under $30 appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Let’s get real for a moment. Most golfers, and by “most,” I mean players with an 18 handicap or higher, probably aren’t reaping the full benefits of a premium golf ball. Expensive balls tend to cater to better players who rely on specific performance characteristics. Taking advantage of those features often requires a combination of higher swing speed, consistent contact and the ability to control launch and spin.

Knowing and accepting that, the good news is that most recreational players don’t need to absorb the added cost of premium golf balls. There are plenty of excellent options for less money that still provide the feel, distance and spin better suited to the recreational player.

Golf.title: New DPWT schedule will force fascinating Ryder Cup decision
Golf.summary: The DP World Tour's new schedule features several fascinating changes — including the Irish Open, national opens and Ryder Cup strategy. The post New DPWT schedule will force fascinating Ryder Cup decision appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
The DP World Tour released its 2027 schedule on Wednesday — and it featured a few notable changes. There are some big-time additions. The Singapore Open (in April, now presented by Deutsche Bank) and the Hong Kong Open (in October) will be co-sanctioned with the Asian Tour. LIV Golf had played events in both places several times in recent years; their realignment with the DP World Tour is a story in and of itself.

The Open de Portugal (in May) also returns to the schedule for the first time since 2020 and adds to the DP World Tour’s roster of historic national opens. Those national opens have been a major focus of the tour as it seeks to double down on the significance and meaning of its global calendar. (The DPWT has been referring to itself as “Golf’s Global Tour,” including in this new schedule release.)

Golf.title: Why the winningest golf ball on the 2026 PGA Tour is 7 years old
Golf.summary: Titleist, to the surprise of no one, dominated the winning golf ball counts in 2026, but it was a ball from 2019 that actually led the way. The post Why the winningest golf ball on the 2026 PGA Tour is 7 years old appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
No one should be surprised that Titleist again led the counts for the PGA Tour’s winningest golf balls this year. The company counted 26 victories during the 2026 FedEx Cup season, more than all the other brands combined and more than six times as the second-place brand. All of those victories were recorded by variants of the flagship Pro V1 and Pro V1x golf balls.

But what’s really interesting and unique about Titleist is that many Titleist golf ball users are playing an older model that Titleist continues to manufacture for them. That’s not because they feel like the new model isn’t better, it’s just different enough that they prefer to stick with what’s comfortable.

Golf.title: AI golf commentator weathers harsh reviews. Its creator responds
Golf.summary: The reviews are in for AI golf analyst Duff Foreman, and they have not been kind. One of Duff’s creators weighs in on the bot's debut. The post AI golf commentator weathers harsh reviews. Its creator responds appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Among the many understandable reasons to fear the rise of AI — security threats, wealth concentration, existential risk — the emergence of golf’s first autonomous tournament commentator probably should rank low on the list of concerns. Still, in pockets of the golf world, the introduction of just such a chatterbot has stirred up agita and scorn. A sampling of golf-observer commentary from the complaint box known as X:

The lamest broadcasters in golf can rest easy, AI slop has made their job is safe. How about we f—ing send this straight into space with a one way ticket. The teeth-gnashing and eye-rolling began last week when Troon Golf distributed a press release about the 2026 New Mexico Open, slated for Sept. 14-16 at Turtleback Mountain Golf & Resort in Elephant Butte, about two hours south of Albuquerque. The event, which is run by the Sun Country Section of the PGA of America, has three former PGA Tour winners in the field, Notah Begay III, Matt Every and Sean O’Hair, but drew buzz not for who would be on the course but in the booth: Ryan Burr, who you might know from Golf Channel, alongside Begay, who would be Ping-Ponging between playing and commentating, and — the real attention-grabber — a new-to-the-scene broadcaster named Duff Foreman.

Villas — from two-story layouts to single-level residences over 4,000 square feet — open floor-to-ceiling to let island breezes do the cooling. Designer kitchens, private plunge pools, and a golf cart come standard, but it’s the indoor-outdoor flow, tuned to the tropics, that makes this feel like a luxurious tree-house stay.

Golf.summary: PGA Tour CEO Brian Rolapp on Tuesday called out "three things" all players, including potential LIV returnees, will need to play on Tour. The post For potential LIV returnees, PGA Tour CEO identifies 3 keys for path back appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Brian Rolapp says he’s been keeping up with current events. But any news the PGA Tour’s CEO had regarding a potential accelerated return of LIV Golf players to his tour was only old news.

In announcing details of a new format coming to the PGA Tour in 2028, Rolapp said Tuesday that the PGA Tour would not re-introduce its “Returning Member Program” to bring back one-time Tour pros who had joined LIV. Rolapp had also said that last month at the Tour Championship, but in the weeks since, LIV has filed for bankruptcy, leading to speculation that its players may be seeking to leave.

Golf.title: PGA Tour says no to shortcut for LIV Golf stars like Jon Rahm, Bryson DeChambeau to return
Golf.summary: PGA Tour says no to shortcut for LIV Golf stars like Jon Rahm, Bryson DeChambeau to return usatoday.com
Golf.body:
The PGA Tour's CEO said the tour is not considering another returning member program for former LIV Golf players, reinforcing the likelihood that stars Bryson DeChambeau and Jon Rahm won't be eligible to return to full-time PGA Tour membership status before 2028.

Brian Rolapp, speaking for the first time since LIV Golf officially entered into bankruptcy proceedings in federal court, told reporters on Tuesday, Sept. 15, the PGA Tour is not offering the path Brooks Koepka used to come back from LIV Golf before the 2026 season. Rolapp emphasized meritocracy, membership rules, accountability and discipline as "guiding principles for us," as the PGA Tour transitions to a new competition model after next season.

Golf.body:
No, Jon Rahm says, he isn’t “fed up” with being asked about LIV Golf. No, he said, he still couldn’t reveal whether he could leave LIV, outside of saying “there’s a long legal process.”

But no, he said, he probably won’t be involved in “the politics of the game” going forward. Speaking Tuesday ahead of this week’s BMW PGA Championship on the DP World Tour, Rahm said that’s been a lesson learned, and it comes as LIV, the tour on which he’s played since 2024, seeks to stay alive following the departure of its primary backer, the Saudi Arabia Public Investment Fund.

Golf.title: At one of golf's most unique events, 80 juniors get a shot on the big stage
Golf.summary: This week, 80 First Tee participants and 80 PGA Tour Champions pros will team up to compete for the title at the Pure Insurance Championship. The post At one of golf’s most unique events, 80 juniors get a shot on the big stage appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
This week, Pebble Beach hosts one of the coolest events in golf — and most people don’t even know it’s happening. The PURE Insurance Championship gets underway at one of golf’s most iconic venues on Friday, bringing together one of the most unique fields you’ll see all season. Here’s what you should know about it.

This week, 80 First Tee participants, 80 PGA Tour Champions pros and 160 amateurs team up to compete in a 54-hole best-ball format for the pro-junior title. For most of the non-pros, it will be their first time playing Pebble Beach, and they come from all over the states — 52 First Tee chapters from across the country have sent players to compete.

Golf.title: Don't make this crucial set-up mistake when hitting bunker shots
Golf.summary: In the first episode of Top 100 Teacher Sessions, David Armitage explains how to set up for success in the bunkers. The post Don’t make this crucial set-up mistake when hitting bunker shots appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
The bunker is a scary place for many recreational golfers. When players with a bunker-phobia find the sand, they typically have one thought in mind: “Don’t screw this up.” The problem with that mindset is that it introduces doubt and leads to hesitant swings, which is never a good strategy in the trap.

The reason for their doubt and hesitation is a history of poor play from the sand. When you’ve spent your career either blading it long or chunking it in front of your feet, there’s little reason for optimism.

Golf.summary: PGA Tour chief executive Brian Rolapp says there are no plans to create an instant pathway back for LIV Golf's biggest stars after the breakaway series filed for bankruptcy protection.
Golf.body:

Major winners Jon Rahm, Bryson DeChambeau and Cameron Smith are contemplating their futures after LIV filed for bankruptcy protection last week as the breakaway league tries to create a new circuit for next year.

Golf.title: Rules Guy: Do I get free relief if my ball hits a fake bird?
Golf.summary: What should you do if your ball hits a bird decoy on the course? Are you entitled to free relief? Rules Guy has the answer. The post Rules Guy: Do I get free relief if my ball hits a fake bird? appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
The Rules of Golf are tricky! Thankfully, we’’e got the guru. Our Rules Guy knows the book front to back. Got a question? He’s got all the answers. To scare waterfowl away from the lake shores, our course uses fake birds on slender poles attached by string and wire that can “fly” with the breeze—soaring, dipping, turning, and so on. A few of these fake birds can be in the line of play from a tee box or near a green. What happens if a shot hits one of these “birds”? It is possible to take the pole out of the ground, play the shot, and replace the pole before hitting, though this can slow the pace of play quite a bit. Movable obstruction? Immovable? Help! —Bill Spahn, via email

You’re trying to sneak in a multipart question, Bill! We’re almost rooting for the waterfowl at this point. As to the first question, if you play near one of those “birds” and hit one, you’ll have to play the ball as it lies — no different than bouncing off a moving cart or a stationary pole, per Rule 11.1.

Golf.title: PGA Tour rules out return programme for LIV Golf players after bankruptcy protection filing
Golf.summary: PGA Tour rules out return programme for LIV Golf players after bankruptcy protection filing The Independent
Golf.body:
There are currently no plans for a route allowing LIV Golf players to return to the US-based PGA Tour, Commissioner Brian Rolapp stated on Tuesday, ruling out a mechanism similar to the one that enabled Brooks Koepka to rejoin earlier this year.

Speaking to journalists during a virtual media call one week after LIV Golf filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in New Jersey, Rolapp insisted that discipline and accountability are vital components for any sporting league and remain core guiding principles for the PGA Tour.

Golf.title: The reason why LIV Golf's future is holding up a DP World Tour pathway to the PGA Tour's new model
Golf.summary: The reason why LIV Golf's future is holding up a DP World Tour pathway to the PGA Tour's new model Golf Digest
Golf.body:
There was a lot of specificity in the PGA Tour’s Tuesday announcement about future membership criteria towards its two-tiered future. Which made the lack of information towards one group somewhat noteworthy.

The PGA Tour is five years into a strategic alliance with its European counterpart, the DP World Tour, a move largely made to financially support the Old World circuit following the pandemic while combating the looming threat of LIV Golf. An upshot of that agreement was a pathway for the top 10 DP World Tour members to graduate to the PGA Tour, an exemption that has been used by the likes of Robert MacIntyre, Min Woo Lee, Matthieu Pavon and Rasmus Hojgaard.

Badminton.title: Asian Games: Smooth Start for Malaysia
Badminton.summary: Asian Games: Smooth Start for Malaysia BWF
Badminton.body:
Malaysia didn’t break a sweat as they overcame Hong Kong China 3-0 in the opening round of the women’s team event of the 20th Asian Games. Letshanaa Karupathevan put the Malaysians on the right track with a 21-9 21-16 result over Lo Sin Yan Happy, before Pearly Tan/Thinaah Muralitharan made it 2-0 beating Yeung Nga Ting/Yeung Pui Lam 21-11 21-17.

Wong Ling Ching then wrapped it up beating Liang Ka Wing in the second singles, 21-17 21-14, sealing a quarterfinals spot for Malaysia against Korea. Two other teams in action on the day – Indonesia and India – too had comfortable victories over Mongolia and Kazakhstan respectively.
