Badminton.title: Humans of Shuttle Time: Ricardo Flores Gómez
Badminton.summary: Humans of Shuttle Time: Ricardo Flores Gómez BWF
Badminton.body:
This is the 74th story in our Humans of Shuttle Time series, in which we present the perspectives of those who are involved with badminton at the grassroots level. Ricardo Flores Gómez, Shuttle Time Teacher with Badminton Federation of Mexico, talks of his journey in badminton.

I grew up in a lower middle class family. I first played badminton at the age of 12 in a sports centre called Agustín Millán Viveros. However, due to family reasons, we moved to Michoacán, and I stopped playing badminton for many years. It was 13 years later that badminton returned to my life when I entered university.

Badminton.title: Korean Women Dominate Early At BWF China Masters
Badminton.summary: Korean Women Dominate Early At BWF China Masters Evrim Ağacı
Badminton.body:
The 2026 BWF China Masters in Shenzhen, China, kicked off with a bang as Korean women’s singles shuttlers An Se-young, Kim Ga-eun, and Shim Yu-jin all stormed into the round of 16, each delivering commanding performances in their opening matches. The tournament, a Super 750 event running from September 1 to September 6, has already seen its share of drama and upsets, with Korea’s top women shining while the country’s leading men’s doubles pair suffered a shock early exit.

World number one An Se-young wasted no time in asserting her dominance. Facing Taiwan’s Lin Xiang-ti in the round of 32, An put on a clinic, winning 2-0 (21-11, 21-3) in just 33 minutes. The match saw An steadily pull away, building momentum with a series of runs—she broke a 9-8 deadlock in the first game with four straight points and then sealed the deal in the second with relentless attacking play, surging to an 11-1 lead and never looking back. It was another display of the form that saw her claim a flawless victory at last month’s World Championships in New Delhi, where she didn’t drop a single game en route to the title.

Badminton.title: BWF Regional Coalition Updates - September 2026
Badminton.summary: BWF Regional Coalition Updates - September 2026 Utah State University
Badminton.body:
September Newsletter for the Utah Women & Leadership Project at Utah State University. In the Bolder Way Forward (BWF) Framework, grassroots is key to making long-term societal change, and that means getting the message to every community, neighborhood, and family in Utah. Leaders and supporters across Utah ensure this happens. The following are quarterly updates for each BWF Region. Please click on the individual County Coalition webpages (linked below) to learn more.

Daggett, Duchesne, Summit, Uintah and Wasatch Counties continue to foster meaningful collaboration, strengthen community partnerships, and advance local efforts across the Uintah Basin, Wasatch, and Summit County regions. With direction from BWF’s Movement-Wide Awareness Campaigns, each coalition creates unique social media posts as they share UWLP and BWF posts. As local leadership transitions, the Daggett, Duchesne and Uintah coalition is seeking new community leads and working to restart the Lunch and Learn series now that the school year is underway. Wasatch County leaders are working with local public radio station KPCW to gather community perspectives for a series of pieces and online articles examining women’s experiences with domestic violence and navigating the judicial system. They are working with partners, including the Peace House, to bring an event to Wasatch County in October, recognizing Domestic Violence Awareness month. Summit County leaders attended the June workshop “Your Strengths, Utah’s Future: Building a State Where All Can Thrive” where networking opportunities arose. They continue to work to rebuild engagement amongst the coalition members, reconnecting with community partners while they identify opportunities to strengthen participation and restore momentum. To get involved, contact Jayden Sillert, UWLP East Central Regional Coordinator.

Badminton.title: History Watch: Two Museums, Two Approaches
Badminton.summary: History Watch: Two Museums, Two Approaches BWF
Badminton.body:
August was a good month for the conservation of badminton heritage, with two museums opening in Europe just a day apart – one in Germany, the other in Denmark. Quite significantly, they are the first badminton museums in either country.

Badminton Museum Bonn, located in the premises of Badminton Club Beuel (Germany’s biggest club), showcases the personal collection of former players and history enthusiasts Helga and Roland Maywald, and opened on 29 August. While most badminton museums celebrate the competition aspect of the sport (players, tournaments), the Maywalds’ collection is devoted to preserving badminton’s presence in the everyday lives of people over the past few centuries, through historical artefacts such as porcelain figurines, postcards, paintings, etc.

Badminton.title: ‘I Want to be a Legend’
Badminton.summary: ‘I Want to be a Legend’ BWF
Badminton.body:
Winning, and making history along the way, has become almost routine for An Se Young. The world No.1 has already collected seven individual titles this season, putting her on course to eclipse the record-equalling 11 she won last year. Yet, she heads into next week’s Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games with her focus firmly on the next match rather than the numbers piling up behind her.

“Records make you a legend. I want to be a legend in badminton,” An said. “But also, they mean you keep improving yourself. So it makes me more motivated. “I always think I can improve further because my rivals could catch up and overtake me. I never take any match for granted.”

Competitor News.title: Deutsche Bank links up with Singapore Open in four-year title partnership
Competitor News.summary: Deutsche Bank links up with Singapore Open in four-year title partnership sportsmintmedia.com
Competitor News.body:
Deutsche Bank has signed a multi-year agreement to become the title partner of the Singapore Open through 2029, giving the historic Asian golf tournament a major international financial-services brand as it returns to the DP World Tour schedule in 2027.

The tournament will be renamed the Deutsche Bank Singapore Open from next season and will be played at Sentosa Golf Club’s The Serapong course from April 15–18, 2027. The event will be jointly sanctioned by the DP World Tour and Asian Tour and will form part of the DP World Tour’s 2027 Asian Swing and the opening phase of the Race to Dubai.

Competitor News.title: Sentosa to Host 2027 Deutsche Bank Singapore Open Under Landmark DP World Tour and Asian Tour Partnership
Competitor News.summary: Sentosa to Host 2027 Deutsche Bank Singapore Open Under Landmark DP World Tour and Asian Tour Partnership Golf Industry Asia
Competitor News.body:
The Deutsche Bank Singapore Open will return to Sentosa Golf Club’s Serapong course from 15–18 April 2027 as a co-sanctioned event between the DP World Tour and Asian Tour. The announcement confirms Sentosa’s continued status as one of Asia’s leading championship venues. Earlier in 2026, the club hosted three major championships, including the Singapore Open, within an eight-week window. The course has long been recognised for its championship conditioning, Tournament Ready 365 (TR365) agronomy programme and industry-leading sustainability practices.

The Singapore Open first came to The Serapong on the Asian Tour in 2005, when Adam Scott claimed the first of his three titles there. Between 2009 and 2012 the event was co-sanctioned by the European Tour (now DP World Tour) and Asian Tour. After a four-year absence, the tournament returned to Sentosa in April 2026.
